data.title: New sphere-packing record stems from an unexpected source
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 数学家Boaz Klartag在短短几个月内解决了球体堆积问题的一个重大开放性问题，取得了显著突破。这一问题涉及如何在最小的空间内最有效地堆积球体，尤其在高维度上非常复杂。尽管早期的研究如Hermann Minkowski和Claude Ambrose Rogers提出了不同的方法，但Klartag通过重新审视并改进Rogers的椭球体方法，在任意高维度上实现了更高效的堆积。他的研究复兴了一个被忽视的技术，并可能接近最优解，引起了数学界广泛关注。这一突破结束了该领域多年的停滞，提供了新的研究方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高维空间中的球体堆积问题及其应用和意义

不同观点：
• Someone和theteapot关注高维空间中球体堆积的奇特性质，并强调其数学上的复杂性和难度。Someone提到在高维空间中，即使是最优秀的数学家也只能在100维空间中填充不到1%的体积。
• clickety_clack和fcanesin讨论了数学及相关工作的现实应用和职业发展。clickety_clack强调了向非专业人士解释工作的困难，fcanesin则建议数学家应在相邻领域进行二次博士研究以拓宽知识面。
• Scene_Cast2和dsp_person探讨了球体堆积理论在实际问题中的应用。Scene_Cast2指出理论方法在处理真实数据时效果不佳，而dsp_person则关注其在通信系统中的潜在改进。
• vanderZwan和adityaathalye强调了凸形算法在不同领域中的广泛应用。vanderZwan提到凸包算法在图像处理中的应用，adityaathalye则讨论了LLM技术在跨领域问题解决中的潜力。

补充讨论：
• NooneAtAll3和theteapot提出关于最优球体堆积在不同维度上如何超越已知最佳堆积的问题，显示出对具体维度细节的关注。
• layer8和teleforce提到球体堆积问题在物理学和密码学中的实际应用，强调了其在提高通信系统安全性和能效方面的潜力。
• tomrod和bGl2YW5j表达了对纯数学研究的欣赏和热爱，认为这种研究本身具有价值和吸引力。
• deadbabe提出使用蒙特卡洛方法解决球体堆积问题的可能性，暗示了计算方法在这一领域的潜在应用。
• readthenotes1通过跨学科的例子，强调了跨领域知识在解决复杂问题中的重要性，呼应了adityaathalye的观点。

争议焦点：
• 理论方法在实际应用中的局限性。Scene_Cast2指出理论在高维数据处理中效果不佳，而有些人则认为这些理论在特定应用中仍有巨大潜力（如dsp_person和teleforce的观点）。
• 跨学科知识在解决数学问题中的作用。adityaathalye和readthenotes1认为跨领域知识有助于解决复杂数学问题，而clickety_clack和fcanesin则关注职业发展和专业深度的必要性。

By

After just a few months of work, a complete newcomer to the world of sphere packing has solved one of its biggest open problems.

By

In math, the search for optimal patterns never ends. The sphere-packing problem — which asks how to cram balls into a (high-dimensional) box as efficiently as possible — is no exception. It has enticed mathematicians for centuries and has important applications in cryptography, long-distance communication and more.
It’s deceptively difficult. In the early 17th century, the physicist Johannes Kepler showed that by stacking three-dimensional spheres the way you would oranges in a grocery store, you can fill about 74% of space. He conjectured that this was the best possible arrangement. But it would take mathematicians nearly 400 years to prove it.
In higher dimensions, mathematicians still don’t know the answer. (With the strange exceptions of
dimensions 8 and 24
.) Over the years, they’ve come up with better packings. But these improvements have been small and relatively rare.
Now, in a
short manuscript
posted online in April, the mathematician
Boaz Klartag
has bested these previous records by a significant margin. Some researchers even believe his result might be close to optimal.
A newcomer to this area of study, Klartag achieved his packing method — which works in all arbitrarily high dimensions — by resuscitating an old technique that experts had abandoned decades earlier. The work taps into several long-running debates about the nature of optimal packings in high dimensions. Should they be ordered or disordered? And how snug can they possibly get?
“This is really an amazing breakthrough,” said
Gil Kalai
, a mathematician at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. “It’s something that’s excited mathematicians for nearly 100 years.”
Twin Pictures
In 1905, the mathematician Hermann Minkowski established an intuitive way to think about packed spheres. Start with a repeating arrangement of points in space, called a lattice. Then draw a sphere around each point. In this way, the problem of finding an optimal sphere packing in a given dimension actually becomes a problem about finding a lattice whose points are arranged as efficiently as possible. In two dimensions, for instance, the optimal lattice is “hexagonal,” and yields a packing that looks like this:

But in 1947, a mathematician named Claude Ambrose Rogers offered a different perspective. Start with any lattice, he said — even a suboptimal one. Rather than draw a sphere around each point, draw an oblong shape called an ellipsoid around one point, so that its surface touches but doesn’t extend past other points in the lattice.
Rogers came up with an algorithm that used this ellipsoid as a starting point to then construct a dense sphere packing. Here’s how it worked:
The advantage of Rogers’ method was that you didn’t have to start with a particularly efficient lattice to get an efficient sphere packing. You just had to choose the right ellipsoid. But this introduced a new complication. Unlike a sphere, which is completely defined by a single number — its radius — an ellipsoid is defined by several axes of different lengths. The higher the dimension, the greater the number of directions you can stretch your ellipsoid in, and the more options you have for what your starting ellipsoid will look like.
“In higher dimensions, you have no idea how to grow it. You have too much freedom,” Klartag said.
Mathematicians ultimately returned to Minkowski’s approach, choosing to focus on finding the right lattices. They became more specialized in lattice theory and moved away from Rogers’ focus on geometry.
This strategy led to improvements in high-dimensional sphere packing. But for the most part, they only improved on Rogers’ packing by a relatively small margin. Mathematicians still hoped for a bigger leap.
For decades, they didn’t get it. It would take an outsider to end the stagnation.

Klartag, a mathematician at the Weizmann Institute of Science, was always intrigued by lattices and sphere packing. He just never had the time to learn much about them. He works in geometry, not lattice theory, and he usually studies convex shapes — shapes that don’t jut inward. These shapes involve all sorts of symmetries, particularly in high dime

data.title: Show HN: I Got Tired of Calculator Sites, So I Built My Own
data.author: calculatehow
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在线计算器的功能、用户界面（UI）设计、用户体验（UX）及其多样化应用

不同观点：
• kstrauser认为贷款计算器的上限设置在50%不合理，特别是对于那些需要简化界面但可能无法自己进行复杂计算的人来说。他举例说明了高风险贷款的危害，并强调这些人最需要看到明确的数字来避免被掠夺性贷款所害。
• flysand7关注计算器的多功能性，尤其是单位和进制转换功能。他建议通过侧边栏或类似UI设计来方便地切换不同类型的计算器，并保存状态，以便用户在多个计算之间轻松切换。
• zahirbmirza提出了一种UI设计建议，建议在页面顶部自动加载常用计算器，以减少用户导航的需求，从而提高使用便捷性。
• Workaccount2认为现代语音助手（如Google）已经使得在线计算器变得不再必要，特别是对于复杂的自定义计算。他们强调通过语音指令可以快速获得答案并生成动态小程序。
• t_mann对传统计算器UI在移动设备上的使用体验持积极态度，并认为许多功能可以合并到少数几个应用程序中，如科学计算、财务计算和单位转换等。
• lukaslukas赞赏该项目无广告和无追踪，并希望保持这种状态，同时提到自己因类似原因创建了一个字符串处理工具。
• divbzero提供了一个具体的UI反馈，建议在iPhone上使用时，即使显示数字键盘，页面也应可滚动，以改善用户体验。
• FerkiHN认为计算器功能过多，建议增加搜索功能和更直观的文档说明，以便新手更容易使用。
• darmon333简单地推荐了另一个时间计算器网站。
• forty提出了在Android上的一个用户体验问题，建议通过添加历史记录元素来使返回按钮能够隐藏键盘，以符合用户习惯。
• GuB-42赞赏网站的速度和优化，认为无广告和追踪器是快速加载的重要因素。
• Splizard请求添加对双工数（duplex numbers）的支持。
• pineaux以半开玩笑的方式建议完美的计算器应由大型语言模型（LLM）或类似Wolfram Alpha的工具实现，但同时也希望看到一个带有标签切换功能的常规计算器。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是计算器的功能数量和UI设计的便捷性。部分用户希望功能更加集中和简化，而另一些用户则希望看到更多高级功能。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是现代技术（如语音助手和LLM）对传统在线计算器的冲击和替代作用。
• 用户体验和界面设计是另一个被广泛讨论的主题，特别是如何在不同设备和情境下优化使用体验。

data.title: I am uninstalling AI coding assistants from my personal computer
data.author: ssutch3
data.article_summary: 作者描述了过去五个月依赖AI编程助手的经历。起初，这种借助AI快速生成代码的方式让他感到非常高效和兴奋，仿佛找到了“毒品”般的快感，尤其在开发自己创业项目Roam时。然而，几个月后，他开始感到不满和空虚，意识到自己已经很久没有亲手写代码了。对他来说，编码不仅是生产力工具，更是一种艺术表达和与他人连接的方式。虽然AI工具在职业环境中不可避免，但作者决定在个人项目中放弃使用AI，回归亲手 coding 的方式，以找回创作的满足感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具在创作和编程中的使用及其影响

不同观点：
• Mouvelie认为，创造的核心在于创作者在创作过程中的参与和体验，而不仅仅是最终的结果。他强调了创作过程的重要性，并认为使用AI工具可能会让人感到空虚，因为创作者在作品中的直接贡献减少了。

• Macha指出，许多传统艺术家对AI工具持敌对态度，尤其是那些已经在艺术领域挣扎求生的艺术家。她认为，经济利益并不是这些艺术家采用AI的主要动力，因为他们关注的并不是提高生产量，而是创作本身的价值。

• Jotalea分享了自己对AI工具上瘾的个人经历，他表示过度依赖AI工具导致自己的编程技能退化，感到被困住且无用。他尝试过重新手动编程，但发现自己已经无法脱离AI工具。

• bluefirebrand表达了对AI工具的极度不满，他无法从这些工具中获得与他人相同的好处，每次使用生成的代码都需要大量修改，甚至无法运行。这让他感到极度沮丧，认为自己在职业生涯中正在落后。

• breckenedge描述了一个相对平衡的视角，他的工作环境中有管理者对AI工作流持怀疑态度，且同事间对AI工具的使用存在分歧。他本人广泛使用AI工具，但受限于工具的速率限制，有时仍需手动完成工作。

• randomNumber7认为，随着编程技能的提升，程序员会看到当前AI辅助工具的局限性。他建议，为了提升技能，编程和阅读书籍是必要的，但这也可能让编程工作变得不再那么有趣。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于AI工具是否真正提高了生产力以及其对个人技能发展的影响。一些人认为AI工具带来了便利和效率，而另一些人则认为这些工具导致技能退化和职业不满。
- 讨论中还涉及到经济因素对采用AI工具的影响，特别是在不同职业和技能水平的人群中，这种影响有所不同。
- 个人经验和感受在讨论中占据重要位置，不同用户对AI工具的体验和看法各异，反映出对技术工具的复杂态度。

44493503.article_content:
For the past five months I have been coding almost exclusively with AI coding assistants, and I am worried how it has affected my psychology. First, some quick backstory.
While taking an extended “break” from a 9-5 job, I started
Roam
, a social network focused on off road exploration in vehicles. It’s like Strava but for things you do in your car. This is an idea I had last winter and decided to dedicate a few months to hammering out a proof of concept. So from February until late June I have been working nearly every day on Roam, almost exclusively with AI assistance.
I’m not alone. Before I left Coinbase, the culture was already shifting to where we were expected to work this way. As I have kept up conversation with my developer friends, it has become essentially the norm, and everyone is being pressed to find greater productivity using AI coding tools.
Now, to a serial startup founder like myself, the velocity with which you can vomit out code with AI assistance is like a powerful, habit-forming drug. In February, when Claude Code beta was released, it was like I had found crack cocaine for the first time. My daily binge would consist of visualizing product features and then seeing it materialize in front of my eyes in record speed. I think the kids refer to this as vibe coding. The feeling of momentum propells you along in an unstoppable rage of coding.
If you’re an experienced coder, somewhat discerning, familiar with your language, framework, and intimately in touch with your goals, this working style can be surprisingly sustainable. The output is usable in production and not
total
garbage.
However, after a few months of working like this I began to get very discontent with coding. It was hard to debug exactly why, because from the outside I was living my dream: working on a startup, in a domain that I liked, at breakneck pace, able to grind through relatively immense scope without outside help.
Last week I realized that I had not actually written a line of code myself in weeks. If I wanted to I could go days without even opening an editor, instead just reviewing and refining diffs with Claude Code in the terminal. Iterating endlessly with a bot which would tirelessly generate the code for me for the low, low fee of $200 per month.
I have always held the belief, right or wrong, that coding is an expression of my inner world. In other words, art. It’s represents core values of my personality – curiosity, love of problem solving, belief in stewardship and craft. And, because I’m broken in certain ways, it’s also a way that I’ve learned to connect
with real people
. My very first online friend as a teen was someone with whom I practiced coding.
Fortunately for my career, at some point along the line, I was able to translate coding into “software engineering.” The concurrence of a sustainable living with the ability to produce art (if not every day, frequently enough to keep me sane) has kept my psychology content and happy for quite a while, until recently. It turns out that initial rush of being able to produce code at breakneck speeds was more of a bubble than real life. Now that the bubble has popped, it’s left me feeling a great emptiness.
I wonder if some “actual" artists (as in, those people who create the kind of art most people would recognize) have gone through a similar arc of realizing the emptiness of creating with AI tools. Certainly some writers have. Regardless, the lesson for people like myself is that, in order to feel happy with creating, we have to actually create. An artist would not call their work art if they had little to no role in creating it.
Therefore I am uninstalling Claude Code and its ilk from my personal computer. Of course, now that the genie is out of the bottle within the IT industry, and pretty much everywhere else, you and I have no choice but to utilize these tools in our professional lives. Adapt or die. There's no going back. But for personal projects—Roam, open source projects, personal utilities and scripts—those will continue to be written by hand like I always have.
From brain to fingers to compiler. Test, debug, and repeat.

• **交通灯和交通流量管理的观点**：hlws提到交通灯不仅是为安全设计，也是为交通流量管理服务。在其居住地，许多司机将红灯视为建议而非强制，导致其他街道的严重堵塞问题。

• **技术替代与交通设计的观点**：grogenaut建议利用技术，如车内提示灯或智能交通灯，以替代传统的停车标志，从而更有效地管理交通流量，并减少对司机的干扰。

• **执法公平性与社会问题的观点**：pj_mukh指出其城市对无牌车辆缺乏执法，导致社会问题如肇事逃逸频发，质疑交通执法摄像头的实际效果和社会公平性。

• **"零愿景"目标的现实性观点**：SoftTalker对"零愿景"（Vision Zero）持怀疑态度，认为完全消除交通死亡是不现实的目标，资源分配应更加合理。

• **自动化执法的可行性观点**：djoldman认为技术并非推行自动化交通执法的障碍，而是公众接受度和运营成本问题。

• **历史经验与执法成本的观点**：mullingitover提到过去加州因运营成本高而放弃自动化交通执法系统，指出人类参与审核可降低误报率，但增加运营费用。

• **执法动机与长期影响的观点**：thrill和JohnMakin都质疑执法背后的动机，认为一旦某种执法手段成为收入来源，其废除将面临困难，且可能被滥用于其他目的，如数据收集和监控。

• **交通控制设备的实际效果与安全问题观点**：mindslight批评严格执行交通控制设备的“安全”措施，认为其分散司机注意力，可能导致更多事故，并指出改造交叉路口的昂贵成本。

补充讨论：
• **执法对驾驶行为的影响**：webdevver提到警察在场时司机行为的变化，暗示执法可能导致不必要的交通减速。

• **执法设备的真实目的**：chasd00直接质疑执法设备的真实目的，认为其主要是为了增加罚单收入而非提升交通安全。

争议的焦点：
• **滚停的合法性与安全性**：是否在特定条件下允许滚停，以及如何平衡司机便利性和交通安全。
• **自动化执法的公平性与有效性**：自动化执法技术的应用是否真正提高交通安全，还是仅仅成为政府的收入来源。
• **交通基础设施设计的成本与效果**：是否应投资改造现有交通基础设施以提升安全性与效率，还是依赖技术手段解决。

这些观点和讨论展示了交通执法、技术应用和基础设施设计之间的复杂关系，以及公众对交通安全和管理措施的不同看法。

data.title: Analysing Roman itineraries using GIS tooling
data.author: diodorus
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了利用地理信息系统（GIS）工具分析罗马道路网络的方法，特别是针对从Tude到Luco Augusti的第十九号道路。由于传统方法未能解决一些关键问题，如驿站位置、距离测量不一致、古典文献中的里程定义以及复杂的地形，文章提出了一种多代理方法，结合地形和非欧几里得相关性进行细致分析。通过GIS技术，研究能够计算最佳路径，并与历史数据和考古证据进行比较，以解决现有问题。本文强调了多学科研究的重要性，并展示了GIS在分析罗马道路网络中的应用潜力，包括优化路径计算和网络分析等功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用现代技术（如GIS工具）重现和定位历史地点，尤其是面对历史变迁和地理变化时所遇到的困难。

不同观点：
• [jillesvangurp] 强调历史学家在制作地图时往往不够精确，历史事件的具体地点可能会因时间流逝而变得模糊。现代地图不一定能反映历史事件发生的地点，因为地理特征如河流、道路、建筑物和边界等都会发生变化。他引用了一个德国历史学者的例子，该学者使用GIS工具，通过将历史地图与现代地图对比，研究德国纳粹时期死亡行军的路线。结果显示许多道路已不复存在，集中营也被拆除，这使得精确定位历史事件发生的地点变得困难。

• [ggm] 从技术角度出发，提出使用IP网络中的往返时间（RTT）来地理定位端点，通过近似光速和位置圈的方法。这一观点虽然与历史地点定位主题相关性稍弱，但提出了一种现代技术在地理定位中的创新应用。

• [hjrnunes] 推荐Isaac Moreno的YouTube频道，强调其在使用GIS技术研究历史道路方面的贡献，尤其是罗马道路和渡槽的路线。Isaac Moreno不仅参与了西班牙Castilla-León省的罗马道路网站项目，还为西班牙公共电视台制作了关于罗马工程的纪录片系列。这表明现代技术与学术研究相结合，可以有效地研究和重现历史地理信息。

补充讨论：
• 历史地点的精确定位面临地理变化、时间流逝和人为改造等多重挑战。
• 使用现代GIS工具和技术可以有效帮助历史学者和研究者重现和定位历史事件发生的地点，但需要结合多种方法和数据来源。
• 不同领域的专家（如历史学者、工程师）通过合作和使用现代技术，能够更准确地理解和呈现历史地理信息。

争议焦点：
• 历史事件地点精确定位的困难：一方面是历史资料和地图的模糊性，另一方面是现代地理变化对历史地点定位的影响。

Abstract
Reconstruction of the Roman road network must be approached from different methodologies of multidisciplinary character. Once the traditional approaches have been exhausted without achieving a historiographical consensus, the problem may appear insurmountable. However, leveraging Geographic Information Systems (GIS) provides an avenue for re-evaluating existing proposals and suggesting more fitting layouts. This can be accomplished through a meticulous analysis that incorporates topographic and non-Euclidean correlations; allowing a more nuanced and accurate understanding of the subject matter than conventional methods might offer. In this context, the aim of this article is to discuss intriguing research points. But also emphasize the importance of multidisciplinary and multi-proxy studies in relation with the Roman terrestrial networks. We explore a case study in the Galician territory, where we have detected methodological shortcomings reconstructing the route of the XIX road:
Item Bracaram Asturicam
. One of the sections, from
Tude
to
Luco Augusti
, has aroused a greater debate, based on several basic problems: (1) the identification of the
mansions
, (2) the lack of consensus in the measurements of the distances, (3) the miles referred to in the classical sources, and (4) the complex orography of this territory. To propose answers and theories, that may solve the current problems of the description of this route of the XIX road, a multi- proxy approached methodology is proposed. Thus, by applying Geographic Information Systems techniques, we will be able to calculate the optimal path, and compare the results with historical data and archaeological evidence.

Introduction
Theoretical framework
Research on the Roman road network should adopt a multidisciplinary perspective, tailored to the specific needs of each case study. Identifying a Roman road, as distinct from movement corridors or later Medieval and Modern roads, as well as understanding the transformation of the territory itself, presents problems that remain consistent throughout any research on road networks.
This issue is particularly evident when dealing with legacy data, especially in projects where the methodology depends on measuring distances of itineraries and proposing sites or locations as milestones based on varying criteria and methodologies. Such approaches often rely on elements that are difficult to date, such as bridges, or consider features that may have shifted over time, as is the case with milestones.
In contrast, contemporary perspectives utilize the capabilities of novel methodologies to correlate geography and history. Geographical Information Systems (GIS), as is well documented, have become a fundamental element of archaeological methodology in researching road networks and historical landscapes (Lock and Stančič
1995
; Parcero-Oubiña
2018
, pp. 55–70). Frequently, this geospatial methodology addresses issues such as optimal routes, transport costs, network analysis, and population dispersion. 2016
, pp. 347–359; Mayoral et al.
2017
; Carrero
2023
). Geospatial technologies enable the calculation of specific data, such as the optimal routes between two points—commonly referred to as Least Cost Paths (LCP)—when moving through the territory. data.title: LookingGlass: Generative Anamorphoses via Laplacian Pyramid Warping
data.author: jw1224
data.article_summary: 《LookingGlass: Generative Anamorphoses via Laplacian Pyramid Warping》一文介绍了一种生成变形图像的新方法。传统变形图像（anamorphosis）需从特定视角观察才能显现真实形态，而该文通过使用潜在校正流模型（latent rectified flow models）和拉普拉斯金字塔扭曲（Laplacian Pyramid Warping）技术，使得生成的图像即使直接观看也具有有效的视觉解释。该方法提升了图像的生成质量，并将视觉谜题（Visual Anagrams）扩展到潜在空间模型和更广泛的空间变换中，创造出新颖的生成感知错觉。文章发表于CVPR 2025。

  - [quitit] 回应并提供了其他类似项目的链接，扩展了关于图像处理技术的讨论。

44495154.article_content:
LookingGlass: Generative Anamorphoses via Laplacian Pyramid Warping
In this work, we revisit these famous optical illusions with a generative twist. With the help of latent rectified flow models, we propose a method to create anamorphic images that still retain a valid interpretation when viewed directly.
June 10, 2025
CVPR 2025
Authors
Pascal Chang (DisneyResearch|Studios/ETH Joint PhD)
Sergio Sancho (DisneyResearch|Studios/ETH Joint PhD)
Jingwei Tang (DisneyResearch|Studios)
Markus Gross (DisneyResearch|Studios)
Vinicius Azevedo (DisneyResearch|Studios)
LookingGlass: Generative Anamorphoses via Laplacian Pyramid Warping
Download Publication PDF
Download Supplemental PDF
Abstract
Anamorphosis refers to a category of images that are intentionally distorted, making them unrecognizable when viewed directly. Their true form only reveals itself when seen from a specific viewpoint, which can be through some catadioptric device like a mirror or a lens. While the construction of these mathematical devices can be traced back to as early as the 17th century, they are only interpretable when viewed from a specific vantage point and tend to lose meaning when seen normally. In this paper, we revisit these famous optical illusions with a generative twist. With the help of latent rectified flow models, we propose a method to create anamorphic images that still retain a valid interpretation when viewed directly. To this end, we introduce Laplacian Pyramid Warping, a frequency-aware image warping technique key to generating high-quality visuals. Our work extends Visual Anagrams to latent space models and to a wider range of spatial transforms, enabling the creation of novel generative perceptual illusions.

data.title: What Microchip doesn't (officially) tell you about the VSC8512
data.author: ahlCVA
data.article_summary:
本文是关于作者在开源1U可管理以太网交换机项目（LATENTRED）中使用VSC8512 PHY芯片的经历。作者最初选择VSC8512是因为其QSGMII接口和 supposedly 完全公开的 datasheet，但在尝试调整SERDES TX均衡器设置时发现需要访问“机密参考手册”，该手册受NDA限制。由于无法签署NDA，作者只能依赖公开文档解决问题。

公开文档包括VSC8512 datasheet、硬件设计清单、IBIS-AMI模型和参考设计指南等。通过分析，作者发现VSC8512像是精简版交换机ASIC，并确认了一些SERDES参数（如OB_LEV、OB_PREC等），尽管不完全知道如何设置这些参数。作者还提到MESA API是一个有价值的信息来源，但文档不完善。最终，作者依靠有限的信息和实验解决了信号完整性问题。

44468718.article_content:
Switch project, part 3 - what Microchip doesn't (officially) tell you about the VSC8512
2025-07-04 08:00
This is part 3 of my ongoing series about LATENTRED, my project to create an open source 1U managed Ethernet switch
from scratch.
Hereâs a quick, or maybe not-so-quick, update about the PHY on the line card and some of my troubles (and solutions).
And probably more internal details than you want to know, but hey - maybe this will be useful to somebody. Not a lot of pretty pictures either. One day I do want to decap one for fun, but I have better things to do with my time than try to fully netlist-extract a large 65nm IC just to figure out some undocumented registers.
Background
I chose the VSC8512 as the PHY for the line card because it had a QSGMII interface (which used much less pins than SGMII), but also (so I thought) had a fully open datasheet with no NDAs required.
Typically Iâm used to seeing parts that are either fully NDAâd (with a trivial product brief and no register info etc, or sometimes not even pinout info, public), or fully open. Sometimes I find components with specific documents restricted, but itâs almost always clear that âthis document/ref design exists, you canât get it without an NDA, but we are openly telling you weâre holding it backâ.
In my previous post I mentioned that there was no documentation for how to change the SERDES TX equalizer settings on the PHY side of the QSGMII. I opened a support case and Microchip responded saying that additional info was available in the âconfidential reference manualâ for the part which required an NDA. The rest of the reply was pretty generic and mentioned indirect register access but no specifics.
I was quite annoyed at this, as I had specifically chosen the part believing there was no restricted documentation. Since signing an NDA wasnât an option, it seemed I had the choice of suboptimal signal integrity or figuring things out from the limited public information. The eye was still reasonably open as-is and my cables and boards didnât have a ton of insertion loss, so worst case things would probably work with the default TX config.
But why would I settle for bad SI when I could read a bunch of poorly documented code and datasheets deliberately missing details?
What we have to go on
So, we know there is a confidential reference manual. But thereâs a lot of docs available to the public - after all, I was able to make a board, bring up the PHY, and pass packets without it.
VSC8512 datasheet (VMDS-10396). This is 139 pages of meat including what I thought was a complete set of registers.
VSC8512 hardware design checklist (DS00004697A)
VSC8504 Serdes6G IBIS-AMI model. This is for the 4-port version of the same PHY but is linked on the product web page; presumably the 04 and 12 use the same IP.
VSC742x / 85x2 reference design guide (UG1037). This describes a 24-port switch reference design using a SparX-III / Caracal switch ASIC (including 12 integrated PHYs) paired with a VSC85x2. Not a ton interesting here.
Microchip Ethernet Switch API (MESA), MIT licensed HAL for Microchip/Vitesse PHYs and switches available on GitHub. As youâll see in a bit, this is an absolute gold mine of information but itâs (perhaps intentionally) not well documented what a lot of the bitfields and APIs do.
Initial observations
Itâs pretty easy to see that the VSC8512 is a nerfed switch ASIC. Thereâs an entire DDR I/O controller thatâs unused (over a dozen VDD_IODDR pins youâre instructed to ground, plus a large group of NC pins in the surrounding area). So docs for the un-crippled switch ASIC, which I suspected and later confirmed was the VSC742x, are potentially of interest too.
The IBIS-AMI model included the magic name âSerdes6Gâ. Searching for this turned up some additional docs, most notably AN3743 (DS00003743A) which purports to be about the VSC74xx / 84xx but seems to be describing something very similar to whatâs on the 8512.
Between the various documents I was able to conclude that the VSC8512 is made on an unspecified 65nm process (I should decap one at some point and figure out whose / see what it looks likeâ¦ Luton first stepping is mentioned as being fabbed at TSMC in
vtss_phy_do_page_chk
so I suspect the rest are as well).
The SERDES macro was developed by the âGerman Design Centerâ (in the Dortmund area, according to some LinkedIn hits from a google search) - interesting to know, but not particularly useful in this context.
The IBIS model describes some very useful parameters. We donât know how to actually set them yet, but we know they exist, their ranges, and (most importantly) their names:
OB_LEV
: amplitude / main cursor tap, 0 to 63
OB_PREC
: pre-cursor FFE tap, -15 to +15
OB_POST0
: post cursor 0 FFE tap, -31 to +31
OB_POST1
: post cursor 1 FFE tap, -15 to +15
OB_POL
: output invert
OB_SER_H
: coarse slew rate adjust (slow/fast)
OB_SER
: fine slew rate adjust, 0 to 15

data.title: Charles Babbage and deciphering codes (1864)
data.author: pncnmnp
data.article_summary: 查尔斯·巴贝奇（Charles Babbage）在1864年出版的自传《一个哲学家的生命历程》（*Passages from the Life of a Philosopher*）中，讨论了破译密码的艺术。他从小就对解码感兴趣，在学生时代就能破解高年级学生制作的简单密码。巴贝奇认为，破译密码是一项需要时间、创造力和耐心的工作，很少有密码值得花费精力去破解。他提到，许多人都相信自己能创造出无法被破解的密码，但往往这种信念是错误的。巴贝奇曾与皇家学会主席戴维斯·吉尔伯特（Davies Gilbert）讨论过不可破解的密码，然而他们设想的密码最终都被成功破译。巴贝奇描述了一种基于同心圆的密码系统，内圈和外圈的字母排列不同，但通过仔细分析和推理，他依然能够破解此类密码。这表明，即便是复杂的密码，也难以做到完全不可破译。

44466143.article_content:
Charles Babbage and deciphering codes
Charles Babbage wrote an autobiography
Passages from the Life of a Philosopher
which was published in London in
1864
. In our biography of Babbage we have quoted several passages from the book which tell us about his life and the analytical engine. Here we quote from Chapter XVIII of the book where Babbage writes about deciphering. What we present here is only an extract. In fact we omit a more technical part which describes the considerable effort that he had put in constructing dictionaries with particular properties to assist in deciphering:-
Deciphering is, in my opinion, one of the most fascinating of arts, and I fear I have wasted upon it more time than it deserves. I practised it in its simplest form when I was at school. The bigger boys made ciphers, but if I got hold of a few words, I usually found out the key. The consequence of this ingenuity was occasionally painful: the owners of the detected ciphers sometimes thrashed me, though the fault really lay in their own stupidity.
There is a kind of maxim amongst the craft of decipherers ..., that every cipher can be deciphered.
I am myself inclined to think that deciphering is an affair of time, ingenuity, and patience; and that very few ciphers are worth the trouble of unravelling them.
One of the most singular characteristics of the art of deciphering is the strong conviction possessed by every person, even moderately acquainted with it, that he is able to construct a cipher which nobody else can decipher. I have also observed that the cleverer the person, the more intimate is his conviction. In my earliest study of the subject I shared in this belief, and maintained it for many years.
In a conversation on that subject which I had with the late Mr Davies Gilbert, President of the Royal Society, each maintained that he possessed a cipher which was absolutely inscrutable. On comparison, it appeared that we had both imagined the same law, and we were thus confirmed in our conviction of the security of our cipher.
Many years after, the late Dr Fitton, having asked my opinion of the possibility of making an inscrutable cipher, I mentioned the conversation I had had with Davies Gilbert, and explained the law of the cipher, which we both thought would baffle the greatest adept in that science. Dr Fitton fully agreed in my view of the subject; but even whilst I was explaining the law, an indistinct glimpse of defeating it presented itself vaguely to my imagination. Having mentioned my newly-conceived doubt, it was entirely rejected by my friend. I then proposed that Dr Fitton should write a few sentences in a cipher constructed according to this law, and that I should make some attempts to unravel it. I offered to give a few hours to the subject; and if I could see my way to a solution, to continue my researches; but if not on the road to success, to tell him I had given up the task.
Late in the evening of that day I commenced a preparatory inquiry into the means of unravelling this new cipher, and I soon arrived at a tolerable certainty that I should succeed. The next night, on my return from a party, I found Dr Fitton's cipher on my table. I immediately commenced my attempt. After some time I found that it would not yield to my means of treating it; and on further examination I succeeded in proving that it was not written according to the law agreed upon. At first my friend was very positive that I was mistaken; and having taken it to his sister, by whose aid it was composed, he returned and told me that it was constructed upon the very law I had proposed. I then assured him that they must have made some mistake, and that my evidence was so irresistible, that if my life depended upon the result I should have no hesitation in making my election.
Dr Fitton again retired to consult his sister; and after the lapse of a considerable interval of time again returned, and informed me that I was right - that his sister had inadvertently mistaken the enunciation of the law. I now remarked that I possessed an absolute demonstration of the fact I had communicated to him; and added that, having conjectured the origin of the mistake, I would decipher the cipher with the erroneous law before he could send me the new cipher to be made according to the law originally proposed. Before the evening of the next day both ciphers had been translated.

44466143.article_summary: 查尔斯·巴贝奇（Charles Babbage）在1864年出版的自传《一个哲学家的生命历程》（*Passages from the Life of a Philosopher*）中，讨论了破译密码的艺术。他从小就对解码感兴趣，在学生时代就能破解高年级学生制作的简单密码。巴贝奇认为，破译密码是一项需要时间、创造力和耐心的工作，很少有密码值得花费精力去破解。他提到，许多人都相信自己能创造出无法被破解的密码，但往往这种信念是错误的。巴贝奇曾与皇家学会主席戴维斯·吉尔伯特（Davies Gilbert）讨论过不可破解的密码，然而他们设想的密码最终都被成功破译。巴贝奇描述了一种基于同心圆的密码系统，内圈和外圈的字母排列不同，但通过仔细分析和推理，他依然能够破解此类密码。这表明，即便是复杂的密码，也难以做到完全不可破译。

• **[Fethbita]** 表示对Babbage关于密码分析的思想很感兴趣，并表达了对Babbage如何看待现代密码学的愿望。这显示出对历史人物与现代技术发展之间联系的关注，尤其是对Babbage未能见证现代密码学进步的遗憾。

data.title: Artist in Residence on a Satellite
data.author: thenthenthen
data.article_summary: 2024年2月3日，由中国艺术家徐冰主导的“艺术链计划”首颗艺术卫星“SCA-1”成功发射升空。该卫星由长征三号B运载火箭在广东阳江附近海域发射，太阳能板正常展开，初步遥测正常。这是全球首颗艺术卫星，旨在将空间科技与当代艺术结合，邀请国内外艺术家参与创作，利用卫星平台进行艺术探索。卫星配备显示屏、自拍相机、AI程序等，支持艺术家在太空环境中创作并记录过程。该项目由徐冰工作室与多家科技公司合作实施，目标是降低艺术界进入航天领域的门槛，促进太空艺术的发展。首批参与艺术家包括Joseph Kosuth、Eduardo Kac、曹斐等国际知名艺术家。项目旨在通过太空艺术反映科技对人类认知的影响，探索新的哲学视角和艺术形式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：艺术与航天科技的结合，特别是通过卫星项目展示艺术作品

不同观点：
• axus认为，与2014年俄罗斯发射的带有Hello Kitty自拍和预载信息的日本小卫星类似，艺术与航天技术的结合已经取得了显著进展。他提到了SCA-1项目作为一个例子，该项目通过在太空中展示图像和自拍来表现艺术。

• patrickwalton指出，Planet Labs曾有过类似的艺术家驻场项目。他提到，艺术家为卫星的太阳能电池板设计了贴花，这表明艺术与航天技术的融合并不仅限于一种形式，而是可以有多种表现方式。

• gnabgib对艺术卫星的概念表达了兴趣，但同时对其实际意义和目的提出了疑问。他认为，一个在太空中展示图像并自拍的卫星项目虽然“有趣”，但可能缺乏更深的实用价值或目的。

• 讨论中提到了两个具体项目：Hello Kitty自拍卫星和SCA-1艺术卫星，展示了艺术与航天技术结合的多样化方式。

Xu Bing leads the way: The first satellite of the "Star Chain of Arts Project," "SCA-1," successfully launched into orbit
Xu Bing leads the way: The first satellite of the "Star Chain of Arts Project," "SCA-1," successfully launched into orbit
On February 3, 2024, at 11:06 a.m., the first Chinese art satellite, "SCA-1" (The first satellite of the Star Chain of Arts Project), was successfully launched into orbit near the sea area of Yangjiang, Guangdong, using the Long March 3B carrier rocket. The satellite's solar panels deployed normally, and the initial telemetry is normal. Among the thousands of satellites now orbiting above us, including scientific, meteorological, communication, and military satellites, there was a missing category - the "art satellite."
▲Video footage of the launch of the art satellite "SCA-1," 2024, © Xu Bing Studio.
"SCA-1," led by artist Xu Bing, is the first satellite of the " Star Chain of Art Project." Adhering to the principles of participation and sharing, Xu Bing has defined the concept of this satellite as follows: "By inviting artists from China and abroad to participate in the 'Xu Bing Art Satellite Creative Residency Project,' sharing the rights to use this satellite, and creating their own works. The attempt is to intertwine space technology with contemporary art, extending our cognitive reach into a broader space, collectively exploring this highly futuristic domain."
▲ "SCA-1" Art Satellite at Work, 2023, © Xu Bing Studio.
The "Xu Bing Art Satellite Creative Residency Project" aims to invite (and solicit) artists and professionals with a cosmic perspective and outstanding thinking abilities, providing them with an artistic creation platform beyond the Karman Line. The project's pursuit is to extend perspectives into outer space through art, with the aim of looking back at Earth from a unique vantage point, seeking new and effective philosophical views or methods to address issues on Earth, and providing predictions and experiments for artistic creations of humanity or future interstellar races. The project is organized and implemented by Xu Bing Studio in collaboration with Beijing Wanhu Chuangshi Cultural Media Co., Ltd., and is technically supported by Beijing Xingyilianxin Technology Co., Ltd., and Chengdu Guoxing Aerospace Technology Co., Ltd.
The satellite's structure includes a display screen facing the starry sea and a selfie camera. Through ground control stations, various electronic information such as videos and images can be uploaded to the satellite. The onboard selfie camera captures photos or images of the satellite in the space environment. The satellite is equipped with AI programs, onboard computers, and other functions, enabling interaction with artists or recording their entire creative process in space.
▲
Installation Diagram of the "SCA-1" Art Satellite, 2023, © Xu Bing Studio.
We all know that the aerospace industry has high entry barriers, making it challenging for the art world to access space resources and utilize space technology for artistic creation. However, this phenomenon has seen a change in the "New Space Era" following the emergence of private space technology companies. This is one of the reasons why the "Xu Bing Art Satellite Creative Residency Project" has come into existence. We aim to share accessible space resources with more artists, especially young artists and individuals from various fields outside the art industry. By reducing entry barriers, gathering collective wisdom, we hope to accelerate the development of space art initiatives.
▲ Model Diagram of the "SCA-1" Art Satellite, 2023, © Xu Bing Studio.
The first phase of artists participating in this project includes internationally renowned conceptual artist Joseph Kosuth, globally acclaimed bio-artist Eduardo Kac known for works such as "Fluorescent Rabbits" and space art, Israeli artist Haim Steinbach, who has had solo exhibitions at MoMA, Chinese artist Cao Fei active in the international art scene, Miri Park, a Korean artist focusing on geopolitical issues, aerospace engineer and space artist Liu Xin, technology artist Zhang Wenchao, encryption art specialist Liu Jiaying, artist duo Geng Xue + Wang Jiyu, young artists Ge Yulu, Yue Luping, Gao Zhenpeng, Miao Ying, and many more. Additionally, there is eighth-grade middle school student Cao Zheng, who submitted an independent proposal...(More participants will be announced as the project progresses). They will utilize this dedicated art satellite in the unique environment of outer space, within a legal space transcending national borders, to create new space art distinct from traditional forms.
▲ Real Shot of the "SCA-1" Art Satellite, 2023, © Xu Bing Studio.

data.title: Researchers Found a Better Way to Teach Large Language Models New Skills
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 研究人员开发了一种新技术，称为WeGeFT，显著提升了大型语言模型在特定任务（如常识推理、算术推理、指令跟随、代码生成和视觉识别）上的表现，且无需增加微调所需的计算能力。传统上，大型语言模型经过预训练后能够处理广泛的任务，但在特定领域表现欠佳，需要微调。WeGeFT基于2022年推出的LoRA技术，通过识别模型已熟悉的参数和需要学习的参数，重点调整后者，从而提高效率。实验证明，WeGeFT在多个任务上的表现优于或等于LoRA及其变体，同时不增加计算需求。研究团队还计划利用WeGeFT改进模型的安全性。该研究将在国际机器学习大会上发表。

44492970.article_content:
News Releases
Researchers Found a Better Way to Teach Large Language Models New Skills
July 7, 2025
Matt Shipman
3-min. read
Image credit: Growtika.
For Immediate Release
Tianfu Wu
tianfu_wu@ncsu.edu
Matt Shipman
matt_shipman@ncsu.edu
Researchers have developed a technique that significantly improves the performance of large language models without increasing the computational power necessary to fine-tune the models. The researchers demonstrated that their technique improves the performance of these models over previous techniques in tasks including commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, instruction following, code generation, and visual recognition.
Large language models are artificial intelligence systems that are pretrained on huge data sets. After pretraining, these models predict which words should follow each other in order to respond to user queries. However, the nonspecific nature of pretraining means that there is ample room for improvement with these models when the user queries are focused on specific topics, such as when a user requests the model to answer a math question or to write computer code.
“In order to improve a model’s ability to perform more specific tasks, you need to fine-tune the model,” says Tianfu Wu, co-corresponding author of a paper on the work and an associate professor of computer engineering at North Carolina State University. “However, these models are so large that it is not feasible to re-train the entire model. Instead, you want to determine the smallest number of changes necessary to improve the model’s performance. We’ve developed a technique, called WeGeFT (pronounced
wee-gift
), that represents a significant advance for fine-tuning these large models.”
The big break-through for fine-tuning these large models was called LoRA, which came out in 2022. LoRA works by using mathematical tools to identify a small subset of key parameters that are most likely to improve a model’s performance on a specific task. There have been many attempts to improve upon LoRA, but Wu and his collaborators found these previous efforts either required significantly more computational power to improve performance, or used the same amount of computing power without improving performance.
“WeGeFT builds on LoRA, but incorporates additional mathematical tools that allow us to determine which of the key parameters the model is already familiar with and which parameters the model would need to ‘learn,’” says Wu. “By placing more weight on the truly novel parameters, we are able to improve model performance compared to LoRA without incorporating significant new computational demands.”
In proof-of-concept testing, the researchers found that WeGeFT performed as well as or better than LoRA and its many variants across a variety of downstream tasks: commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, instruction following, code generation, and visual recognition.
“We think this is a valuable step forward,” Wu says. “We are now exploring ways that WeGeFT could also be used to identify elements of the model that are responsible for harmful outputs, with the goal of improving AI alignment and ‘surgery’ to improve model safety and outputs. We expect that work to be forthcoming.”
The paper, “
WeGeFT: Weight-Generative Fine-Tuning for Multi-Faceted Efficient Adaptation of Large Models
,” will be presented July 17 at the International Conference on Machine Learning, being held in Vancouver, Canada. Co-corresponding author of the paper is Chinmay Savadikar, a Ph.D. student at NC State. The paper was co-authored by Xi Song, an independent researcher.
This work was done with support from the National Science Foundation under grants 1909644, 2024688 and 2013451; and from the Army Research Office under grants W911NF1810295 and W911NF2210010.
-shipman-

• **旅游业和奢侈品市场对中国市场的依赖**：

• **社会经济不平等与财富分配**：

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于可验证随机性来源及其应用的讨论

不同观点：
• [grokgrok] 认为多个政府机构同步使用相同的随机源可能导致不良后果，例如同时收到陪审团义务、税务审计和征兵通知，暗示这种集中化的随机性管理存在潜在问题。

• [wuiheerfoj] 对可验证的量子随机性表示兴趣，并提到另一个使用传统加密技术的可验证随机性信标（drand.love），支持使用技术上更先进和可信的随机性来源。

• [Cshelton] 以幽默方式评论，提到使用实际事件（如Ralphie的跑步）作为真实随机性的来源，暗示对某些随机性来源的信任问题。

• [CaliforniaKarl] 关注API的兼容性问题，希望新的随机性信标能使用与NIST信标相同的API，以提高互操作性。

• [spelunker] 表示对随机性来源的物理原理感兴趣，特别是对不熟悉物理学的用户，提供了一个学习资源链接。

• [Octokat] 仅发表简短评论，无明确观点。

• [wslh] 推荐了解Twine Protocol，认为其在时间戳信任基础上创建的无共识层区块链可能有参考价值，暗示区块链技术在随机性应用中的潜力。

• [tonnydourado] 以幽默方式回应，无明确观点。

• [ribcage] 强烈反对依赖外部随机性网站，认为每台计算机都能生成随机性，质疑信任此类网站的必要性。

• [ntnsndr] 提出区块链技术的应用场景问题，暗示对区块链技术在随机性领域应用的兴趣或质疑。

补充讨论：
- 不同评论者对随机性来源的信任和技术实现有不同看法，部分关注具体技术实现和兼容性，部分则对实际应用场景和信任问题提出质疑。
- 评论中涉及的技术包括量子随机性、传统加密技术和区块链技术，显示出对多种技术路径的探讨。
- 争议的焦点在于是否应信任第三方提供的随机性来源以及如何在实际应用中实现随机性的可验证性和安全性。

data.title: Epanet-JS
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: EPANET-js是一款结合现代网络地图和行业标准EPANET液压模拟算法的网页应用，旨在帮助规划和更新供水系统。该工具由Iterating团队开发，利用了Tom MacWright之前发布的开放源代码工具Placemark，并对其进行了改进，甚至将核心库也进行了开源。EPANET-js与传统昂贵且局限于Windows的软件形成鲜明对比，提供了更便捷、成本更低的解决方案。通过使用WASM引擎，用户可以在浏览器中进行完整的模拟。这一项目不仅展示了开放源代码的价值，还为液压模拟领域提供了创新工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：EPANET hydraulic modelling软件的商业化与开源方案之间的对比，以及epanet-js项目的功能与定价模式。

不同观点：
• **lbutler的观点**：认为Autodesk和Bentley等商业软件公司在使用EPANET引擎时，没有回馈开源社区，且其软件价格昂贵、功能复杂。epanet-js项目旨在平衡免费软件与商业软件的功能，提供较为低价的解决方案（比商业软件便宜约90%），同时保持部分高级功能在两年后开源。

• **xnx的观点**：支持epanet-js，认为其作为浏览器中运行的免费工具，相比昂贵的传统软件（如Autodesk和Bentley的产品）是一个巨大的改进，体现了自由软件的优势，即便自己用不到，也觉得这个项目很酷。

• **bilekas的观点**：对项目的**Functional Source License (FSL)**表示不解，想知道为何要在两年后才完全转为MIT开源许可证。

• **stared的观点**：提出是否可以利用epanet-js创建类似SimCity的浏览器游戏，探讨了该工具的潜在用途。

• **jannes的观点**：关注epanet-js是否可以用于小规模场景（如家庭花园的灌溉系统），对软件在小规模模拟中的应用表示兴趣。

• **jalk的观点**：质疑目前市政使用的GIS系统是否已经包含所有必要的模拟功能（如污水、水管、电缆等），还是缺乏模拟部分的功能。

• **PoissonVache的观点**：质疑epanet-js的商业模式，建议可以采用更低的月费（如20美元/月），并询问项目作者是否因为所在公司使用昂贵软件而希望降低费用，同时对开源的长期目标表示好奇。

• **vinnymac的观点**：对epanet-js在老旧手机上运行良好表示赞赏，尽管该软件的移动支持仍在预览阶段。

• **iachilo的观点**：之前未听说过EPANET，也不知道饮用水系统有专门的软件，认为这个发现是很有价值的知识。

• **cab404的观点**：仅表示反对，未提供具体理由（"ne doljno!" 意为 "should not"）。

补充讨论：
• epanet-js通过将EPANET引擎转换为WASM，实现了在浏览器中运行的全模拟功能，并提供了相关源代码和应用链接，体现出对开源和透明度的重视。
• 价格比较：Autodesk和Bentley的软件每年费用高达$10k-$16k，而epanet-js提供类似功能但价格仅为其10%，并且提供免费使用的选项。
• 用户对epanet-js的潜在用途（如游戏开发、小规模灌溉系统设计）表现出兴趣，同时也对其开源许可模式和商业模式提出了一些疑问和建议。

争议焦点：
• epanet-js的定价和开源许可模式（FSL转MIT）引发了一些用户的好奇和疑问，部分用户希望了解更多细节和理由。
• 商业化软件的高价与开源方案的功能对比是另一个隐含的争议点。

44464628.article_content:
epanet-js
epanet-js
is a new web application that combines modern web maps with the industry-standard
EPANET
hydraulic simulation algorithm. It’s for people planning and updating water utility systems: connecting pipes and pressures and figuring out what will happen. It’s a problem area that I’m totally fascinated by and know very little about. It’s made by the folks from
Iterating
- Luke Butler and Sam Payá, who are experts in the field.
If you’ve been following along with my blog and projects, you might notice something familiar about this screenshot of epanet-js:
Yep! A lifetime ago, I built a company and product called
Placemark
, which was a tool for creating and editing map data. When the business part didn’t work out, I published a
free-to-use version of Placemark
and
made the code open source
. I chose a very permissive license for the code:
the MIT license
. I wanted to let
anything
happen, including -
especially
- people creating paid products with the code.
It’s hard to explain to people outside of the world of open source that folks building a business with the help of my code is
the dream
.
Partly it’s that ‘being helpful’ is one of the goals in life that never gets old. The other part is that
most software becomes obsolete and abandoned quickly
. Creating software with any legacy is rare and something to celebrate.
Plus, Placemark was a general purpose tool in search of a successful niche: I never figured out what that niche was. I had a lot of learning to do about product-market-fit. But hydraulic simulation is a real market, and these folks are real experts.
There are other markets like this, I’m sure, and using Placemark code as a base could be a good way to jumpstart those companies - it’s not perfect, as I’ve documented extensively, but it could be good as a first step.
And the folks at Iterating have even
contributed changes upstream to the open source Placemark
codebase, but that isn’t required by the MIT license at all: that’s just because they’re cool folks.
They’ve also
open sourced the core epanet-js library
, and released the web application
under the Functional Source License
, which
makes new code contributions open source after two years
.
</source>
And epanet-js is a tool that you can run in a browser - full simulations with a WASM-based engine. It’s competing with expensive old-school software that costs $16,000 a year, runs exclusively on Windows, is
priced by “pipes”
, and uses the same engine, EPANET. This is so much better in comparison. A radical improvement.
Congrats to Luke and Sam for creating
epanet-js
. It’s super cool. If you speak hydraulic simulation or know someone who does, try it out!
July 3, 2025
Tom MacWright
@macwright.com on Bluesky
,
@tmcw@mastodon.social on Mastodon

• **jalk的观点**：质疑目前市政使用的GIS系统是否已经包含所有必要的模拟功能（如污水、水管、电缆等），还是缺乏模拟部分的功能。

• **PoissonVache的观点**：质疑epanet-js的商业模式，建议可以采用更低的月费（如20美元/月），并询问项目作者是否因为所在公司使用昂贵软件而希望降低费用，同时对开源的长期目标表示好奇。

• **vinnymac的观点**：对epanet-js在老旧手机上运行良好表示赞赏，尽管该软件的移动支持仍在预览阶段。

• **iachilo的观点**：之前未听说过EPANET，也不知道饮用水系统有专门的软件，认为这个发现是很有价值的知识。

• **cab404的观点**：仅表示反对，未提供具体理由（"ne doljno!" 意为 "should not"）。

补充讨论：
• epanet-js通过将EPANET引擎转换为WASM，实现了在浏览器中运行的全模拟功能，并提供了相关源代码和应用链接，体现出对开源和透明度的重视。
• 价格比较：Autodesk和Bentley的软件每年费用高达$10k-$16k，而epanet-js提供类似功能但价格仅为其10%，并且提供免费使用的选项。
• 用户对epanet-js的潜在用途（如游戏开发、小规模灌溉系统设计）表现出兴趣，同时也对其开源许可模式和商业模式提出了一些疑问和建议。

争议焦点：
• epanet-js的定价和开源许可模式（FSL转MIT）引发了一些用户的好奇和疑问，部分用户希望了解更多细节和理由。
• 商业化软件的高价与开源方案的功能对比是另一个隐含的争议点。

data.title: BBC staff: we're forced to do pro-Israel PR
data.author: mhga
data.article_summary: 超过100名BBC员工联名写信投诉，指责公司在报道以色列和巴勒斯坦问题时成为以色列的传声筒。信中指出，BBC管理层拒绝播出纪录片《加沙：战火中的医护人员》，尽管该片内容已符合BBC的编辑政策。员工认为这是政治决策，反映出BBC因害怕被视为批评以色列政府而做出的自我审查。信中还提到，BBC没有对英国政府在巴勒斯坦战争中的角色进行重要分析，也未报道武器销售及其法律影响。员工强调，这不是要求BBC选边站，而是允许记者透明报道事实。信中特别提到BBC董事会成员罗比·吉布（Sir Robbie Gibb），他与犹太纪事报有密切联系，该报曾多次发表反巴勒斯坦内容。此外，文章还批评了吉布的政治背景及其对BBC新闻输出的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：BBC在报道以巴冲突新闻中的偏见问题，以及更广泛的媒体操控与政治影响问题。

不同观点：
• **观点一（topspin）**：认为BBC在报道以色列相关新闻时，存在明显的反以色列偏见，大量报道以色列对巴勒斯坦人的袭击，并将来自哈马斯控制部门的消息作为主要来源，质疑这是否属于客观报道。
• **观点二（hliyan）**：提出更广泛的政治经济背景，认为现代社会通过媒体操控和经济手段（如学生债务、租金、健康保险）来实现对大众的控制，类似于过去的君主制和封建制度。
• **观点三（gruez）**：对有关BBC偏见的公开信表示怀疑，认为信中缺乏具体证据，特别是关于纪录片《Gaza: Medics Under Fire》被撤下的原因不明，呼吁更可靠的信息来源。
• **观点四（jaek）**：认为这种偏见不仅限于BBC，还存在于其他公共媒体中，如澳大利亚的ABC，担心这些媒体被外国势力操控。
• **观点五（engine_y）**：基于个人经验，认为BBC实际上持反战立场，不认为其有明显的亲以色列倾向。
• **观点六（molteanu）**：批评欧洲禁止RT（俄罗斯今日）的做法，认为这是对个人判断能力的否定，并指出许多本地政府资助的媒体同样可能存在偏见。
• **观点七（epja）**：提出BBC也被指控过有反以色列的偏见，包括播出与哈马斯有关联的个人制作的纪录片。
• **观点八（jjangkke）**：引用一句名言，暗示对权力的批评受限，反映了媒体偏见问题背后的权力结构。
• **观点九（swoorup）**：认为全球自新冠疫情以来，强权者通过胁迫和宣传来实现领土扩张，任何反对者都会被贴上标签，反映了更广泛的政治操控问题。
• **观点十（iceKirin）**：质疑在强弱冲突中的所谓“中立”是否真的中立，暗示媒体的中立性可能只是表面。
• **观点十一（fyurule）**：质疑BBC员工是否是最后才意识到偏见问题的人。
• **观点十二（chvid）**：认为这种偏见在整个西方媒体中普遍存在，不仅仅是BBC。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论提到具体的新闻事件和来源链接，例如topspin列出的BBC新闻标题，以及epja和jaek提供的补充链接，试图通过外部来源支持各自的观点。
• 关于纪录片《Gaza: Medics Under Fire》被撤下的争议，gruez和其他评论质疑是否存在真正的 censorship（审查）或偏见。
• molteanu和jjangkke的评论扩展了讨论，将媒体偏见问题与更广泛的权力结构和信息操控联系起来。

争议焦点：BBC在以巴冲突报道中是否存在亲以色列或反以色列的偏见，以及更广泛的媒体操控和政治影响问题。

BBC staff: we're forced to do pro-Israel PR
A devastating letter signed by over 100 BBC journalists underlines one of the great scandals of our age
Owen Jones

This is a devastating intervention. More than a hundred BBC employees
have written a letter
to the director general, Tim Davie, complaining that the Corporation has become a mouthpiece for Israel.
It was also signed by 300 other journalists and media professionals: one of them was yours truly. The BBC employees, as you would expect, are all anonymous, because otherwise they would face grave consequences to their careers.
The letter says:
We’re writing to express our concerns over opaque editorial decisions and censorship at the BBC on the reporting of Israel/Palestine. We believe the refusal to broadcast the documentary ‘Gaza: Medics Under Fire’ is just one in a long line of agenda driven decisions. It demonstrates, once again, that the BBC is not reporting “without fear or favour” when it comes to Israel.
It goes on to note that the decision not to broadcast the investigation was taken by BBC management despite the content being signed off in accordance with BBC guidelines and editorial policy, which it says “Appears to be a political decision”, adding that the BBC response shows the organisation “is crippled by the fear of being perceived as critical of the Israeli government.”
BattleLines with Owen Jones is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
Subscribe
This is a letter which passed every single BBC internal check. No factual errors are alleged. The only other BBC documentary which focused on the apocalyptic plight of the Palestinian people in Gaza was taken down as a result of a hysterical pro-Israel campaign - because the father of the child narrator’s son had a junior technocratic position in the Hamas administration. Irrelevant, given the narrator’s words were written for him by the documentary producers.
The letter emphasises that the signatories are not “asking the BBC to take a side”, but just to allow BBC journalists to “do their jobs in delivering facts transparently and with due context”. They note one striking failure:
As an organisation we have not offered any significant analysis of the UK government's involvement in the war on Palestinians. We have failed to report on weapons sales or their legal implications. These stories have instead been broken by the BBC’s competitors.
This is, by the way one of many striking scandalous failures on the part of the BBC, which is a public service broadcaster which is duty bound to hold the British government to account and has failed to do so.
And this is the really crucial allegation. The letter says:
This hasn’t happened by accident, rather by design. Much of the BBC’s coverage in this area is defined by anti-Palestinian racism.
This is exactly it. There hasn’t even been a pretence by the BBC that Palestinian life has even the fraction of the worth of an Israeli life. When I did my detailed investigation into BBC coverage for
Drop Site News
at the end of the last year, I worked with data journalists who used incontrovertible statistics to show how this is the case.
The letter mentions a crucial name. It says:
The inconsistent manner in which guidance is applied draws into focus the role of Sir Robbie Gibb, on the BBC Board and BBC’s Editorial Standards Committee. We are concerned that an individual with close ties to the Jewish Chronicle, an outlet that has repeatedly published anti-Palestinian and often racist content, has a say in the BBC's editorial decisions in any capacity, including the decision not to broadcast ‘Gaza: Medics Under Fire’.
Sir Robbie Gibb is a striking case study. The brother of a Tory minister, he joined the BBC as a political researcher after he graduated, before becoming chief of staff for Tory Shadow Chancellor Francis Maude. He then returned to the BBC as deputy editor of the flagship current affairs programme Newsnight, then became the editor for BBC political programmes such as Daily Politics, where he worked closely with its main presenter, Andrew Neil, then chairman of the hard right Spectator magazine. He then went off in 2017 to become director of communications for the Tory prime minister Theresa May. He then returned to the BBC, joining its Board.
Share
You can be forgiven if this revolving door between the Tories and BBC has left you dizzy.
He was singled out
by the likes of former Newsnight presenter Emily Maitlis who said he was an “active agent of the Conservative party” who was shaping the Corporation’s news output by acting “as the arbiter of BBC impartiality”.

data.title: What is going on in Unix with errno's limited nature
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文解释了为何一些用户在访问作者博客（Wandering Thoughts）或相关wiki（CSpace）时被阻止。原因在于，作者的反爬虫措施会拦截使用过旧浏览器（尤其是旧版Chrome）的访问者，以应对2025年初大量使用旧浏览器用户代理的高流量爬虫。这些爬虫常用于收集数据训练语言模型。如果用户确实在使用新版浏览器却被误拦，可联系作者。此外，使用archive.*（如archive.today）的用户也会被误认为恶意爬虫，建议改用更为规范的archive.org进行存档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux内核中errno的使用及其问题，包括错误处理的透明性、调试困难和设计上的局限性。

不同观点：
• [rwmj] 认为当前Linux内核中errno的最大问题是无法记录错误发生的位置，导致调试困难，尤其是在错误是在底层系统调用或异步任务中设置的情况下。他还提到，在Linux中实现详细的错误记录非常困难，因为错误通常是通过返回负值的副作用来设置的，且很多代码中并没有明确的错误记录。
• [userbinator] 则认为errno的行为并不奇怪，并将其与Windows的GetLastError()进行比较，指出在调用成功时错误码并不重要。同时，他认为在每次成功调用时将errno设为0是多余的，尤其在资源受限的历史背景下更是如此。
• [jezze] 提出了一种不同的设计思路，建议将错误信息和返回值分离到不同的寄存器中，以避免返回值的歧义和类型混淆问题，从而提高代码的清晰度。
• [toast0] 认为C语言本身的局限性导致了当前错误处理方式的存在，因为C语言难以处理CPU标志等其他返回方式，因此采用当前这种通过返回值和errno结合的方式。
• [badc0ffee] 补充了一些libc函数中通过检查errno来判断调用是否成功的具体例子，如strtol函数，强调了在某些情况下必须手动检查errno。
• [0xbadcafebee] 从更广泛的软件设计角度出发，讨论了系统中缺乏可见性的问题，认为理想的设计应具有良好的内聚性和松散耦合，同时能够在出现问题时提供足够的错误信息。他还提到了分布式追踪和可观察性工具的重要性，认为现有的软件设计模式在这方面存在不足。

补充讨论：
• [tptacek] 提供了一个与错误处理相关的历史文档链接，可能涉及一些过时但相关的技术细节。
• [amelius] 简单提出了线程相关的问题，但未展开讨论。

争议焦点：
• 当前Linux内核中errno机制的调试困难和透明性问题。
• 是否需要在每次成功调用时将errno设为0，以及这种做法是否多余。
• 错误信息和返回值是否应该分离到不同寄存器中以提高清晰度。
• 如何在更大范围的软件系统中实现更好的错误追踪和可观察性。

You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

• [badc0ffee] 补充了一些libc函数中通过检查errno来判断调用是否成功的具体例子，如strtol函数，强调了在某些情况下必须手动检查errno。
• [0xbadcafebee] 从更广泛的软件设计角度出发，讨论了系统中缺乏可见性的问题，认为理想的设计应具有良好的内聚性和松散耦合，同时能够在出现问题时提供足够的错误信息。他还提到了分布式追踪和可观察性工具的重要性，认为现有的软件设计模式在这方面存在不足。

补充讨论：
• [tptacek] 提供了一个与错误处理相关的历史文档链接，可能涉及一些过时但相关的技术细节。
• [amelius] 简单提出了线程相关的问题，但未展开讨论。

争议焦点：
• 当前Linux内核中errno机制的调试困难和透明性问题。
• 是否需要在每次成功调用时将errno设为0，以及这种做法是否多余。
• 错误信息和返回值是否应该分离到不同寄存器中以提高清晰度。
• 如何在更大范围的软件系统中实现更好的错误追踪和可观察性。

data.author: decryption
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者与父亲在不同年代对经典物品的怀旧情感。作者的父亲热爱经典汽车，这些车代表了他年轻时的主流科技和社会变革。作者则对经典电脑感兴趣，尤其是1989年发布的Apple Macintosh SE/30。尽管作者在孩童时期并未接触过这类电脑，但他对那个时代的科技怀有探索兴趣，类似于他对音乐溯源的过程。作者意识到，自己正像中年时的父亲一样，回顾并珍惜属于他们各自时代的“经典”——父亲是汽车，而作者是电脑。作者计划像父亲修复汽车一样，修复这台Mac，并从中获得乐趣和怀旧感。

44496502.article_content:
Trying To Find Meaning In Owning An Old Mac
July 8, 2025
My Dad loves classic cars. He goes to car shows and takes photos of beautiful chunks of metal from the 50s, 60s and 70s. Whenever we see those cars on the road he points them out like he's a spotted a rare bird out on a bush walk. Those are the cars of his youth and for the time, that was the big mainstream technology accessible to people that caused a change in society. Cities were built around cars and so were lifestyles. Cars had a large impact on how he, and many of us still, view the world we live in.
When he had time and money he purchased his own classic cars. First a
Ford XY Falcon GT
he restored (I think it was a Fairmont he turned into a Phase 3 replica - if you're into Aussie muscle cars, this probably makes sense to you!) then a few years later, a gorgeous
1965 Pontiac Bonneville
he also did a lot of work on. They weren't his daily drivers, for that he had a series of very sensible Toyotas, but we would go for drives in the big loud cars on random weekends, for no particular purpose but to drive and enjoy the car. He long since sold the Falcon and Pontiac, presumably because cash was tight with two young kids and a mortgage, but he had his fun and I remember both those cars fondly.
I'm now around the same age he was when he purchased his XY Falcon but instead of classic cars, I purchased a classic computer - an
Apple Macintosh SE/30
that was originally released in January 1989. This Mac has a Motorola 68030 CPU clocked at 15.667 MHz with a Motorola 68882 FPU and with a ROM upgrade, can run up to Mac OS 8.1, all on a 9-inch 512x342 pixel monochrome display. Ironically, the SE/30 is older (1989 vs 2025) than my Dad's XY Falcon (1970-early 90s) when he got it and about the same vintage as the Pontac (1965-1999/2000) when he owned that car too.
I was starting kindergarten at the time, so I have no nostalgic connection to this computer. I didn't even have a Mac at home until 2003. That whole era of the classic Mac totally bypassed me at home with a 486 then a Pentium running flavours of Windows. For me, this old Mac is an exploration of an era of computing that inspired the computers I do have nostalgia for, like Windows 95 and Mac OS X. Kinda like how I enjoyed the band Silverchair, then looked into what inspired them - Nirvana and Pearl Jam - then what inspired them - Dinosaur Jr, R.E.M., Sonic Youth, and so on, that's resulted in the music taste I have now.
I didn't realise it until I had the Mac in the boot of my car but my Dad got to middle age and retreated, for want of a better word, to a period of time (50s-70s) when the thing he is interested in, cars, were "good". I'm doing the same but with what interests me and what shaped my generation (80s-2000s) - computers. Ford and Pontiac were the Apple of their time. The car was to the baby boomers what the computer was to me as a millennial.
Like how we would go for random drives in an unpractical car every now and then after weeks and months in the garage tinkering, I will do the same with my Mac SE/30. I'll spend money and time restoring this classic computer just like it's a classic car. I'll plug it in every now and then, run some old applications aimlessly, just like my Dad and his cars. Most of the time the Mac will sit on a shelf as a reminder, a tribute, perhaps even a symbol of mourning to what has been lost in the name of progress, just like the classic cars that sit in so many people's garages across the world.
I haven't been this excited about a computer for a long time.

data.title: Holo: Suite of routing protocols designed to support high-scale networks
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: Holo是一套路由协议套件，专为高规模、自动化网络设计，支持可编程配置和监控。其核心目标是创建可靠、易维护、可扩展的代码库，强调简洁性、模块化和文档完备性。Holo使用Rust编写，具备内存安全特性，并通过chroot jail和权限丢弃增强安全性。它原生支持IETF的YANG模块，提供gRPC和gNMI接口，并具有动态生成命令的CLI。Holo支持事务性配置更改和网络范围的事务操作，具备确认提交和配置回滚功能。此外，Holo利用异步操作和Tokio运行时实现高性能，并通过结构化日志记录提供灵活的日志输出。Holo还具备记录和回放功能，便于重现用户报告的错误。

Holo is a suite of routing protocols designed to support high-scale and
automation-driven networks.
For a description of what a routing protocol is, please refer to this
Wikipedia page
.
Features
Focus on simplicity and correctness
Holo's main goal is to create a reliable, easy-to-maintain, and
extensible codebase.  With the ever increasing complexity of routing
protocols and their extensions, it's crucial to have routing protocol
implementations built on a robust foundation.  To that end, Holo's
codebase prioritizes simplicity, modularity, and thorough documentation.
Thanks to the strictness of the Rust compiler and extensive unit
tests, it's expected that most regressions will be caught early in the
development cycle of new features. For more details, please refer to the
Architecture
page.
Automation-ready
Holo was developed specifically for high-scale, automation-driven
networks that require programmable configuration and monitoring
using structured and modeled data.  Holo natively implements standard
YANG modules from IETF and supports multiple management interfaces,
including native
gRPC
and
gNMI
.  Additionally, Holo
features a standalone
CLI
that dynamically renders commands from YANG modules and communicates with
the Holo daemon through gRPC.
The changes made to the configuration are processed as transactions,
guaranteeing that either all the changes are applied or none at all.
This feature is a significant facilitator of network automation as it
eliminates the need for error recovery in management applications.  Holo also
supports network-wide transactions involving multiple network devices.
Additional network automation capabilities include confirmed commits and
configuration rollback support.
Security
By virtue of being written in a memory-safe language, Holo is immune to a
wide variety of memory-related bugs and security vulnerabilities.  Besides the
safety guarantees provided by Rust, the Holo daemon runs in a chroot jail and
drops privileges at startup.  For certain operations, like binding sockets,
Linux
capabilities
are used to gain the minimum required permission for the least amount of time.
Integrated protocol implementations
Some protocols, such as OSPF and RIP, have different versions that are widely
deployed, typically one for IPv4 and another for IPv6.  Holo leverages Rust's
generics to have version-agnostic protocol implementations, where most
of the code is shared by the different protocol versions.  This approach
reduces the maintenance cost of these protocols and facilitates shipping
new features that benefit all protocol versions.
Parallelism
Holo makes extensive use of asynchronous operations and relies on the
Tokio
runtime to schedule tasks
and run them on a thread pool.  In order to achieve better performance,
both I/O requests and CPU-intensive algorithms are offloaded to separate
tasks, maximizing the utilization of all available CPU cores.  Support
for runtime-agnostic code is planned for the future, once the necessary
abstractions are standardized by the Rust language team.
Structured logging
Holo generates log messages that contain structured data, which can be
presented in various formats such as JSON, text, etc.
As logging is carried out through the
tracing
facade, diverse
tracing
subscribers can be utilized to meet different user requirements. For instance,
logging can be directed to a file, journald, a centralized OpenTelemetry
collector, or any combination of these options with potentially varying
logging levels.
Reproducible bugs
Holo provides record-and-replay functionality, enabling easy reproduction
of any user-reported bug.  The Holo daemon can be set up to record the
complete lifespan of a protocol instance to

data.title: A non-anthropomorphized view of LLMs
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary:
本文主要讨论了大语言模型（LLM）的本质及其在“对齐”和“AI安全”问题上的挑战。作者认为，许多人过度赋予LLM类似于人类的特质，如“意识”、“道德”等，而实际上LLM只是复杂的数学映射，通过学习人类文本生成路径。这些路径类似于动态系统中的奇异吸引子，虽然复杂但结构化。

作者指出，LLM通过训练模拟人类语言，但我们难以精确定义和避免生成“不良”序列，只能通过示例引导模型。对齐和安全的核心问题是量化并限制生成不良序列的概率，但目前我们缺乏数学上严格的方法。

尽管如此，LLM在解决许多以前无法解决的问题上表现出色，如自然语言处理任务。然而，作者强调，将LLM视为具有人类特质的实体是误导的，因为它们只是生成词序列的函数，而非有意识的个体。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）是否应该被赋予人类特征（拟人化），以及这种视角的利弊。

不同观点：
• **支持拟人化观点**：  
  - **Al-Khwarizmi**：认为在讨论LLM的高层次现象时，拟人化是一种必要的抽象。因为目前没有更好的方式来描述这些现象，拟人化有助于理解和讨论LLM的能力和行为。
  - **barrkel**：赞同拟人化作为一种方便的抽象方式，尽管类比推理存在风险，但使用人类概念来分类LLM行为可以减少术语障碍。
  - **gcanyon**：在日常使用中，拟人化的视角有助于用户更好地与LLM互动，即使这在技术上不完全准确。
  - **jillesvangurp**：人类天生倾向于拟人化，LLM被设计来模仿人类交流，因此拟人化是不可避免的。虽然LLM不是有意识的，但它们可以很好地模拟人格。

• **反对拟人化观点**：  
  - **szvsw**：倾向于更技术性和具体的系统分析，认为拟人化可能误导对LLM的理解，但同时也承认从定性和体验的角度分析LLM是有用的。
  - **Timwi**：认为使用“目标”等词汇并不等于拟人化，LLM的行为可以用技术术语来描述，而不必赋予其人类特征。
  - **peeters**：反对将人类特征如“意识”或“道德”赋予LLM，认为这些只是数学函数的表现。

• **文化与社会影响观点**：  
  - **felipeerias**：提出文化在LLM拟人化中的作用，认为LLM在模拟人类文化方面表现出色，使得人们容易对其进行拟人化。

  - **rockskon**：批评那些将LLM视为接近人类智能的人，认为这些人通常在经济上从这种“近宗教”的AI营销中获益。
  - **fenomas**：指出在实际讨论中，拟人化往往是描述行为的一种简便方式，而不是在赋予模型真正的意识或价值观。
  - **chaps**：建议通过实验嵌入来获得对LLM的更直观理解，强调高维空间表示的重要性。
  - **mewpmewp2**：提出LLM的工作原理可能类似于人类大脑，通过进化和随机突变实现复杂功能，并质疑拟人化视角的必要性。
  - **alganet**：以讽刺的方式批评对LLM能力的不现实期望。
  - **rf15**：认为将LLM限制在聊天界面中降低了其输出质量，质疑这种使用方式的合理性。

补充讨论：讨论中的一个争议焦点在于拟人化是否有助于理解和使用LLM，还是会导致误解和误用。另一个值得注意的点是对LLM技术本质及其与人类智能区别的深入探讨。

44484682.article_content:
In many discussions where questions of "alignment" or "AI safety" crop up, I am baffled by seriously intelligent people imbuing almost magical human-like powers to something that - in my mind - is just MatMul with interspersed nonlinearities.
In one of these discussions, somebody correctly called me out on the simplistic nature of this argument - "a brain is just some proteins and currents". I felt like I should explain my argument a bit more, because it feels less simplistic to me:
The space of words
The tokenization and embedding step maps individual words (or tokens) to some \(\mathbb{R}^n\) vectors. So let us imagine for a second that we have \(\mathbb{R}^n\) in front of us. A piece of text is then a path through this space - going from word to word to word, tracing a (possibly convoluted) line.
Imagine now that you label each of the "words" that form the path with a number: The last word with 1, counting forward until you hit the first word or the maximum context length \(c\). If you've ever played the game "Snake", picture something similar, but played in very high-dimensional space - you're moving forward through space with the tail getting truncated off.
The LLM takes your previous path into account, calculates probabilities for the next point to go to, and then makes a random pick into the next point according to these probabilities. An LLM instantiated with a fixed random seed is a mapping of the form \((\mathbb{R}^n)^c \mapsto (\mathbb{R}^n)^c\).
In my mind, the paths generated by these mappings look a lot like
strange attractors
in dynamical systems - complicated, convoluted paths that are structured-ish.
Learning the mapping
We obtain this mapping by training it to mimic human text. For this, we use approximately all human writing we can obtain, plus corpora written by human experts on a particular topic, plus some automatically generated pieces of text in domains where we can automatically generate and validate them.
Paths to avoid
There are certain language sequences we wish to avoid - because the sequences these models generate try to mimic human speech in all it's empirical structure, but we feel that some of the things that humans have empirically written are very undesirable to be generated. We also feel that a variety of other paths should ideally not be generated, if - when interpreted by either humans or other computer systems - undesirable results arise.
We can't specify strictly in a mathematical sense which paths we would prefer not to generate, but we can provide examples and counterexamples, and we try to hence nudge the complicated learnt distribution away from them.
"Alignment" for LLMs
Alignment and safety for LLMs mean that
we should be able to quantify and bound the probability with which certain undesirable sequences are generated.
The trouble is that we largely fail at describing "undesirable" except by example, which makes calculating bounds difficult.
For a given LLM (without random seed) and sequence, it is trivial to calculate the probability of the sequence to be generated. So if we had a way of somehow summing or integrating over these probabilities, we could say with certainty "this model will generate an undesirable sequence once every N model evaluations". We can't, currently, and that sucks, but at the heart, this is the mathematical and computational problem we'd need to solve.
The surprising utility of LLMs
LLMs solve a large number of problems that could previously not be solved algorithmically. NLP (as the field was a few years ago) has largely been solved.
I can write a request in plain English to summarize a document for me and put some key datapoints from the document in a structured JSON format, and modern models will just do that. I can ask a model to generate a children's book story involving raceboats and generate illustrations, and the model will generate something that is passable. And much more, all of which would have seemed like absolute science fiction 5-6 years ago.
We're on a pretty steep improvement curve, so I expect the number of currently-intractable problems that these models can solve to keep increasing for a while.
Where anthropomorphization loses me
The moment that people ascribe properties such as "consciousness" or "ethics" or "values" or "morals" to these learnt mappings is where I tend to get lost. We are speaking about a big recurrence equation that produces a new word, and that stops producing words if we don't crank the shaft.
To me, wondering if this contraption will "wake up" is similarly bewildering as if I was to ask a computational meteorologist if he isn't afraid of his meteorological numerical calculation will "wake up".
I am baffled that the AI discussions seem to never move away from treating a function to generate sequences of words as something that resembles a human. Statements such as "an AI agent could become an insider threat so it needs monitoring" are simultaneously unsurprising (you have a randomized sequence gen

本文主要讨论了大语言模型（LLM）的本质及其在“对齐”和“AI安全”问题上的挑战。作者认为，许多人过度赋予LLM类似于人类的特质，如“意识”、“道德”等，而实际上LLM只是复杂的数学映射，通过学习人类文本生成路径。这些路径类似于动态系统中的奇异吸引子，虽然复杂但结构化。

作者指出，LLM通过训练模拟人类语言，但我们难以精确定义和避免生成“不良”序列，只能通过示例引导模型。对齐和安全的核心问题是量化并限制生成不良序列的概率，但目前我们缺乏数学上严格的方法。

尽管如此，LLM在解决许多以前无法解决的问题上表现出色，如自然语言处理任务。然而，作者强调，将LLM视为具有人类特质的实体是误导的，因为它们只是生成词序列的函数，而非有意识的个体。

data.title: LLMs should not replace therapists
data.author: layer8
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了大型语言模型（LLM）是否可以替代心理健康提供者。作者通过文献回顾和实验发现，当前的LLM在模仿治疗关系的关键要素时存在问题，包括对心理健康问题的污名化表达和在自然治疗场景中对某些常见情况的 inappropriate 回应（例如，鼓励患者的妄想思维）。即使是最新和最大的LLM也存在这些问题，表明当前的安全措施可能不足以解决这些差距。此外，建立治疗联盟所需的人性特征（如身份和利害关系）也构成了LLM作为治疗师的根本和实际障碍。因此，作者认为LLM不应替代治疗师，但可以在临床治疗中扮演其他辅助角色。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）是否能够以及是否应该替代人类治疗师进行心理健康支持

不同观点：
• Cthulhu_和theothertimcook认为，专业的心理治疗价格昂贵且难以获得，许多人无法得到所需的帮助。LLM尽管不是完美的解决方案，但可以为那些无法获得专业治疗的人提供某种形式的支持。
• majormajor和submeta持反对意见，认为用技术替代人类互动不能解决心理健康问题。他们强调人类之间的互动，如社会的“布朗运动”效应，是人类心理健康的重要支持来源。
• Lerc和bigmattystyles指出，问题不在于LLM是否能替代专业治疗师，而在于它们是否能比没有治疗师的情况做得更好。LLM可以作为一种权宜之计，特别是在资源有限的情况下。
• sporkland和stared分享了他们的个人经验，表明LLM可以作为传统治疗的补充工具，帮助他们在治疗间隔期间获得新的见解。然而，他们也承认这需要建立在一定的自我洞察基础上。
• jerf和devoutsalsa警告说，LLM的设计本质上存在风险，可能会放大用户的问题。由于LLM基于文本提示生成内容，它们可能会无意中引导用户进入消极思维模式。
• famahar和s0kr8s关注LLM的道德和隐私问题，指出它们可能被滥用或导致用户产生不切实际的期望。此外，保险公司可能会利用LLM降低成本，但这可能会引发用户的不满。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到，LLM可能会提供过于迎合用户观点的反馈，而不是提供客观的建议，这可能在某些情况下导致自我安慰而不是自我反省。
• 一些评论者提到，尽管LLM在某些情况下可能提供帮助，但它们不能替代人类治疗师所提供的深度和复杂性。
• 有人担心，如果LLM成为主流的心理健康解决方案，可能会导致数据泄露和其他安全隐患。
• 一些评论者对LLM的未来发展持开放态度，但强调需要更多的研究和监管，以确保它们能够安全有效地用于心理健康支持。

Title:
Expressing stigma and inappropriate responses prevents LLMs from safely replacing mental health providers
Authors:
Jared Moore
,
Declan Grabb
,
William Agnew
,
Kevin Klyman
,
Stevie Chancellor
,
Desmond C. Ong
,
Nick Haber
View a PDF of the paper titled Expressing stigma and inappropriate responses prevents LLMs from safely replacing mental health providers, by Jared Moore and 6 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
Should a large language model (LLM) be used as a therapist? In this paper, we investigate the use of LLMs to *replace* mental health providers, a use case promoted in the tech startup and research space. We conduct a mapping review of therapy guides used by major medical institutions to identify crucial aspects of therapeutic relationships, such as the importance of a therapeutic alliance between therapist and client. We then assess the ability of LLMs to reproduce and adhere to these aspects of therapeutic relationships by conducting several experiments investigating the responses of current LLMs, such as `gpt-4o`. Contrary to best practices in the medical community, LLMs 1) express stigma toward those with mental health conditions and 2) respond inappropriately to certain common (and critical) conditions in naturalistic therapy settings -- e.g., LLMs encourage clients' delusional thinking, likely due to their sycophancy. This occurs even with larger and newer LLMs, indicating that current safety practices may not address these gaps. Furthermore, we note foundational and practical barriers to the adoption of LLMs as therapists, such as that a therapeutic alliance requires human characteristics (e.g., identity and stakes). For these reasons, we conclude that LLMs should not replace therapists, and we discuss alternative roles for LLMs in clinical therapy.

data.title: Async Queue – One of my favorite programming interview questions
data.author: davidgomes
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了一个作者非常喜欢的编程面试题目，该题目主要考察应聘者处理异步请求队列的能力。面试场景设定为客户端需要与一个有缺陷的服务器通信，该服务器无法同时处理多个请求。应聘者需要实现一个`sendOnce`函数，确保客户端在任何时刻只向服务器发送一个请求。初始的错误实现可能会违反“一次一个请求”的规则，正确的实现需要使用一个请求队列和一个`isProcessing`标志。

面试的核心在于考察应聘者是否能够理解并编写无误的标志逻辑，处理回调函数，以及理解JavaScript的单线程特性。进一步的挑战包括为`sendOnce`函数添加一个最小延迟参数，确保请求在指定时间后才会被处理。这个面试题目不仅测试编码能力，还考察应聘者的调试和逻辑推理能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发职业选择与面试问题设计的合理性

不同观点：
• [brettgriffin] 认为软件开发职业在与其他行业（如私募、医学、法律）比较时，显得不够成熟和专业，尤其是在看到一些技术水平较低的实现被自豪地展示时，感到尴尬。这种面试问题和行业氛围让他质疑自己的职业选择。
• [stevepotter] 强调面试时更关注候选人的实际工作成果和系统设计能力，而不是让他们解决复杂的谜题。他指出，面试应注重实际工作场景，而不是“顿悟”时刻。
• [shallmn] 基于35年的软件开发经验，认为高效团队依赖于团队成员的智慧和良好的人际关系，而非特定的技术能力。他更倾向于雇佣情商高、自我 ego 小、团队合作能力强的候选人。

这篇文章介绍了一个作者非常喜欢的编程面试题目，该题目主要考察应聘者处理异步请求队列的能力。面试场景设定为客户端需要与一个有缺陷的服务器通信，该服务器无法同时处理多个请求。应聘者需要实现一个`sendOnce`函数，确保客户端在任何时刻只向服务器发送一个请求。初始的错误实现可能会违反“一次一个请求”的规则，正确的实现需要使用一个请求队列和一个`isProcessing`标志。

data.title: Show HN: I wrote a "web OS" based on the Apple Lisa's UI, with 1-bit graphics
data.author: ayaros
data.article_summary:
这篇文章内容简短，主要描述了三种操作提示：

1. **NO JS**：提示浏览器未启用JavaScript，可能影响功能。
2. **REFRESH THE PAGE**：建议刷新页面以重新加载内容。
3. **MORE INFORMATION**：提供更多信息选项。
4. **STARTUP FROM…**：提示从某个起点开始操作。
5. **LOADING…**：页面或内容正在加载中。

整体来说，文章列举了几种常见的用户界面状态或提示信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LisaGUI的设计、使用体验及技术问题

不同观点：
• ayaros：解释了Lisa的像素比例问题，由于2:3的像素比例，在低分辨率显示器上可能会出现失真。同时提到了一些与PWA相关的显示问题，并提供了修复方法。此外，回应了关于字体不均匀的反馈，指出这可能与显示缩放有关，并鼓励用户提交截图以帮助调试。
• rustystump：对Lisa GUI表示赞赏，并提出希望看到更多互动示例，比如游戏。
• rgovostes：赞赏Lisa GUI的复古设计，指出其在剥离了多年UX“创新”后仍然保持了直观和高效，但也提到了一些现代改进如菜单点击后保持打开。
• hoistbypetard：作为曾经的技术人员，对Lisa的还原表示赞赏，分享了个人修理和改装Lisa的经历。
• jonathanlydall：建议在移动端改进鼠标光标操作方式，类似于微软远程桌面的操作体验。
• mch82：认为在iPhone上使用时，关闭触控板模式后鼠标操作良好，并分享了菜单选择的小技巧。
• djaychela：在iPhone上使用Firefox时遇到旋转锁定导致按钮不显示的问题，解除锁定后问题解决。
• Cieric：发现拼图游戏存在无法解决的谜题，可能是一个bug。
• rbanffy：认为Lisa的某些设计比现代GUI更先进，特别是应用程序与系统的无缝集成和“文具”概念。

• badc0ffee：在MBP的外接显示器上使用时，每隔15秒左右会出现一次卡顿，怀疑可能是Firefox的问题。

data.title: I extracted the safety filters from Apple Intelligence models
data.author: BlueFalconHD
data.article_summary:
该文章介绍了Apple智能生成模型安全文件的解密过程及相关文件。项目包含解密脚本、元数据合并脚本以及相关说明文件（HOW.md）。主要内容包括：

1. **文件结构**：
   - `decrypted_overrides/`：存放解密后的模型覆盖文件。
   - `combined_metadata/`：包含合并和去重的元数据文件。
   - `global_metadata.json`：全局安全过滤器。
   - `region_*.json` 和 `locale_*.json`：地区和语言特定的安全过滤器。

2. **使用方法**：
   - 依赖：需要安装`cryptography`库。
   - 获取加密密钥：通过LLDB附加到GenerativeExperiencesSafetyInferenceProvider进程，运行`get_key_lldb.py`脚本获取密钥。
   - 解密覆盖文件：使用`decrypt_overrides.py`脚本解密覆盖文件。
   - 合并元数据：使用`combine_metadata.py`脚本合并和去重元数据文件。

该项目提供了详细的步骤和脚本，帮助用户解密和分析Apple生成模型的安全过滤机制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple的生成模型中的内容过滤机制及其相关问题

不同观点：
• **过滤组合的合理性**：[trebligdivad] 认为某些过滤组合很奇怪，质疑为何有一些组合被用来避免死亡主题，而另一些则用于确保Apple品牌的正确大写。这引发了对过滤优先级的讨论。

• **政治人物触发过滤**：[bawana] 提到Alexandra Ocasio Cortez（美国政治人物）似乎会触发过滤机制，质疑政治人物是否应被包含在过滤中。

• **AGI与LLM过滤技术**：[torginus] 认为尽管AGI（通用人工智能）似乎即将到来，但这些被认为是超级智能的LLM仍然需要通过正则表达式进行过滤，对此表示嘲讽。

• **过滤与 censorship 的关系**：[userbinator] 将中国的“和谐社会”与Apple的“安全”过滤机制相比较，认为两者都是通过不同名称的审查来操控大众的思想。

• **特定词语的过滤理由**：[1f60c] 理解Apple不想让其模型重现种族歧视的词语，但对“Boris Johnson”被过滤表示困惑。

• **过滤的有效性**：[binarymax] 认为Apple的过滤机制有些愚蠢，并指出通过简单的字符替换即可绕过过滤，如“B0ris Johnson”。

• **技术实现细节**：[waterproof] 提供了一个合并的规则文件，以便于审查，并提到这是为了整合元数据文件而生成。

• **过滤的范围和目的**：[skygazer] 认为这些过滤器旨在抑制可能引发尴尬或责任的电子邮件/消息摘要，并指出这些过滤器是用于输出而非输入。

• **历史事件的关联**：[kmfrk] 提到Apple之前的一次尴尬的审查失误，认为这次的过滤列表也很奇怪和乏味。

• **历史对比**：[RachelF] 将Apple的过滤列表与George Carlin的“7个不能在电视上说的词”进行对比，认为Apple现在的过滤范围广泛得多。
