It seems to have made me an account in both a Firebase instance and a custom database on
catwatchful.pink
.
After registration and login, I get given an APK to download and install. From here, installation goes as usual for Android stalkerware: the app has me download and install another APK pre-configured with my account credentials. This app then asks for basically every permission on the system, guides me through uninstalling the original installer app, then runs in the background forever while disguising itself in the app drawer with a generic “Settings” icon.
Part 1: Recon
#
After installing the app and re-logging into the web interface, I’m presented with a control panel with which to spy on my test phone. Two things stand out to me here: first of all, the app works really well. A lot of stalkerware apps are half-broken, clearly built by gluing together various chunks of spaghetti code long abandoned by their original authors. Not so here - all these features work as advertised with minimal latency. The live photo and microphone options are particularly creepy, successfully taking a photo or recording and uploading it for me to view near-instantly on the control panel without giving the phone user the slightest sign that anything is amiss.
The only bug I found was in the sidebar counters (I did not in fact take 3002 screenshots while testing)
The second notable thing is that all the personal data collected here seems to be stored in Firebase, served from Cloud Storage URLs in the form
catwatchful-e03b8.appspot.com/o/usersFiles/JIOgo826TPfb0pMFKmzkE7jz9JO2/M6GPYXHZ95ULUFD0/micRecorders/grab_2025-06-09_17-04-34
. Intercepting my test phone’s traffic confirms that the files are directly uploaded to Firebase, and reveals that the commands for features like live photos are also handled through FCM. This is going to reduce our attack surface by a lot - nothing in Firebase is going to be IDORable or vulnerable to SQLI, and some quick testing eliminates any of the usual traps like open storage buckets or client-side service account credentials. We’re going to have to focus on that mysterious
catwatchful.pink
server I was also signed up on.
Part 2: Playing with the other server
#
Scrolling back through the requests since I logged back in, I see a few more requests

• **[JohnMakin]**：分享了自己曾遭遇类似问题，手机被零点击漏洞感染，但至今不知道幕后黑手是谁，对恶意软件的开发者和使用者表示强烈反感，认为研究人员的披露过于温和。

• **[blueplanet200]**：引用sqlmap的使用条款，强调未经授权的攻击行为是非法的，并担心作者可能面临法律风险，建议谨慎行事。

• **[ceva]**：认为恶意软件运营者不会起诉研究人员，对法律风险持乐观态度，并赞扬了作者的工作。

• **[esaym]**：对恶意软件的实时照片和麦克风监控功能表示震惊，认为这些功能极其 creepy（令人毛骨悚然）。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Google Play Protect的实际效果和Google托管恶意软件应用的责任问题。
• 另一个焦点是使用sqlmap等工具进行安全测试的合法性问题，部分人担心法律风险，而其他人认为不必担心。

data.title: Brut: A New Web Framework for Ruby
data.author: onnnon
data.article_summary:
Brut是一个简约但功能齐全的Ruby web框架，不同于其他框架，它没有控制器、动词或资源，而是直接构建页面、表单和单一操作处理器。Brut注重低抽象和低仪式感，但并非像Sinatra那样的低级框架。它内置OpenTelemetry仪表盘、基于Sequel的数据访问层以及基于OptionParser的命令行应用。

Brut安装简便，支持Docker快速启动。其核心设计基于类和对象，避免了过多的include和动态方法。它统一了客户端和服务器端表单验证，并通过BrutJS提供自定义元素。使用esbuild处理CSS，无需PostCSS或SASS。

Brut默认设置良好实践，如内容安全策略和数据库非空约束。它使用RSpec进行测试，支持Phlex生成HTML，并避免使用YAML进行配置。Brut简化了开发，消除了不必要的抽象和辩论，让开发者专注于编写Ruby和HTML，享受构建web应用的过程。

接下来，作者将继续完善Brut并发布1.0版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个新web框架的评价与技术实现的讨论，涉及架构设计、技术选择、许可证问题以及与Rails框架的对比。

不同观点：
• **rorylaitila** 认为该框架强调表单和页面，通过表单和链接驱动交互，JavaScript只作为增强工具，控制器被过度使用。他主张用表单、模型（后端）和视图（页面）来处理交互，框架可以帮助简化验证和控制器相关的复杂操作。
  
• **wrs** 没有直接评价技术细节，而是引用了Brut的HIPPOCRATIC LICENSE许可证，强调了在采用技术时应关注道德和伦理问题，尤其是与劳工权益相关的方面。

• **sarchertech** 支持该框架的灵活性，提到如果开发者希望使用函数式编程概念（如monad、代数数据类型等），该框架不会阻碍。该框架适合小型项目或由高级开发者组成的团队使用。

• **freedomben** 认为该框架是Sinatra和Rails之间的良好折中，适合那些不需要Rails复杂性的简单应用，期待尝试。

• **raggi** 将该框架与Camping框架对比，指出其没有动态父类构造器，暗示其设计更为简洁。

• **heeton** 提到在尝试登录示例站点时遇到了错误，表明在身份验证过程中出现了问题。

• **hamzakc** 建议考虑使用Roda而不是Sinatra，暗示Roda可能更适合该框架的需求。

• **gavmor** 对命名和资源路径设计提出疑问，认为虽然设计简单直接，但可能在具体实现上仍有不确定性。

• **cosmojg** 同样关注许可证问题，详细引用了HIPPOCRATIC LICENSE的条款，强调其对商业行为的限制，特别是涉及人权和公平待遇的部分。

• **caseyohara** 持怀疑态度，认为虽然减少Rails的样板代码有吸引力，但对于大型项目，样板代码不可避免，且Rails的约定和规范有助于团队协作和代码维护。对于小型项目或个人项目，可以打破常规，但对于商业应用，规范和约定是必要的。

补充讨论：
- 许可证的道德和伦理问题成为部分讨论者的关注点，尤其是对开发工具的供应链和劳工权益的考量。
- 不同开发者对框架的简洁性、灵活性和约定规范的重要性有不同看法。一些人认为减少样板代码和约定是优势，另一些人则认为约定和规范对大型项目的可维护性至关重要。
- 对框架具体实现（如资源命名、路径设计）也存在一定的争议，部分开发者对其设计选择提出疑问。

44502463.article_content:
Brut
aims to be a simple, yet fully-featured web framework for Ruby. It's different than other Ruby web frameworks.  Brut has no controllers, verbs, or resources. You build pages, forms, and single-action handlers. You write HTML, which is generated on the server. You can write all the JavaScript and CSS you want.
Hereâs a web page that tells you what time it is:
class
TimePage
<
AppPage
def
initialize
(
clock
:)
@clock
=
clock
end
def
page_template
header
do
h1
{
"Welcome to the Time Page!"
}
TimeTag
(
timestamp:
@clock
.
now
)
end
end
end
Brut is built around low-abstraction and low-ceremony, but is not low-level like Sinatra.  Itâs a web framework. Your Brut apps have builtin OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation, a
Sequel
-powered data access layer, and developer automation based on
OptionParser
-powered command-line apps.
Brut
can be installed right now, and you can build and run an
app in minutes. You donât even have to install Ruby.
> docker run \
-v "$PWD":"$PWD" \
-w "$PWD" \
-it \
thirdtank/mkbrut \
mkbrut my-new-app
> cd my-new-app
> dx/build && dx/start
> dx/exec bin/setup
> dx/exec bin/dev
# => localhost:6502 is waiting
Thereâs a full-fledged example app called
ADRs.cloud
you can run right now and see how it works.
What You Get
Brut has extensive documentation
, however these are some highlights:
Brutâs core design is around classes that are instantiated into objects, upon which methods are called.
No excessive
include
calls to create a massive blob of functions.
No Hashes of Whatever. Your session, flash, and form parameters are all actual classes and defined data types.
Minimal reliance of dynamically-defined methods or
method_missing
.  Almost every
method
has documentation
.
Brut leverages the modern Web Platform.
Client-side and server-side form validation is unified into one user experience.
BrutJS
is an ever-evolving
library
of autonomous custom elements AKA web components to progressively enhance your
HTML.
With
esbuild
, you can write regular CSS and have
it instantly packaged, minified, and hashed. No PostCSS, No SASS.
Brut sets up good practices by default.
Your app will have a reasonable content security policy.
Your database columns arenât null by default.
Your foreign keys will a) exist, b) be indexed, and c) not be nullable by
default.
Time, available through Brutâs
Clock
, is always timezone-aware.
Localization is there and is as easy as we can make it. We hope to make it easier.
Brut uses awesome Ruby gems
RSpec is how you write your tests. Brut includes custom matchers to make it
easier to focus on what your code should do.
Faker and FactoryBot will set up your test and dev data
Phlex generates your HTML. No, we wonât be supporting HAML.
Brut doesnât recreate configuration with YAML.
I18n uses the
i18n gem
, with translations
in a Ruby Hash
. No YAML.
Dynamic configuration is in the environment, managed in dev and test by
the
dotenv gem
. No YAML.
OK, the dev environmentâs
docker-compose.dx.yml
is YAML. But thatâs
it
.
YAML, not even
once
twice.
Brut doesnât create abstractions where none were needed.
Is this the index action of the widgets resource or the show action of the widget-list resource?
is a question you will never have to ask yourself or your team. The widgets page is called
WidgetsPage
and available at
/widgets
.
My
Widgets
class accesses the
WIDGETS
table, but it also has all the domain logic of a widget!
No it doesnât.
DB::Widget
gets your data.  You can make
Widget
do whatever you want. Heck, make a
WidgetService
for all we care!
What if our HTML had controllers but they were not the same as the controllers in our back-end?
There arenât any controllers. You donât want them, you donât have to make them.
What about monads or algebraic data types or currying or maybe having everything
be a
Proc
because
call
?!
You donât have to understand any part of that question.  But if you want your business logic to use functors, go for it. We wonât stop you.
WHY?!?!?!
I know, we can vibe away all the boilerplate required for Rails apps.  But how much fun is that?  How much do you enjoy setting up RSpec, again, in your new Rails app? How tired are you of changing the âfront end solutionâ every few years?  And arenât you just
tired
of debating where your business logic goes or if itâs OK to use HTTP
DELETE
(tunneled over a
_method
param in a
POST
) to archive a widget?
I know I am.
I want to have fun building web apps, which means I want write Ruby, use HTML, and leverage the browser. Do you know how awesome browsers are now?  Also, Ruby 3.4 is pretty great as well. Iâd like to use it.
What I
donât
want is endless flexibility, constant architectural decision-making, or pointless debates about stuff that doesnât matter.
I just want to have fun building web apps.
Next Steps
I will continue working
toward a 1.0 of Brut
, building web apps and enjoying the process.  I hope you will, too!
Promotion
Fix Your Dev Environment for Good

data.author: skeptrune

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个开源的jukebox项目引发的多方面讨论，包括功能改进建议、法律许可问题、公平性讨论以及与其他类似服务的比较。

不同观点：
• **功能改进建议**：
  - **andelink**：建议扩展到YouTube以外的媒体服务，比如通过Odesli（前song.link）整合Apple Music、Spotify等平台，允许用户直接分享这些平台的链接。
  - **foresto**：建议支持作为shoutcast流播放，让用户可以通过常规音响系统收听，而不是仅限于网页浏览器。
  - **corny**：建议在最后一个歌曲播放结束后，保持播放模式，以便新添加的歌曲能立即播放；同时希望不仅播放音频，还能播放视频。

• **法律及许可问题**：
  - **extraduder_ire**：指出项目中MIT许可证未被正确放置到license.txt文件中，仅在readme中提及是不够的。
  - **cdurth**：担心从YouTube抓取视频并存储到S3上可能导致YouTube API密钥被撤销以及遭遇DMCA（数字千年版权法）问题。

• **与其他服务的比较**：
  - **Unai**：提到另一个存在多年的“Jukebox”服务，质疑是否存在关联或者只是名字和功能上的巧合。
  - **itslennysfault**：将该项目与deepcut.live（前turntable.fm）进行比较，认为该项目是更简约和开源的版本。
  - **Aeolun**：提到Grooveshark关闭后，依然怀念其上的epicpower群组，并分享了相关链接。
  - **jason_zig**：提到另一个类似的服务JQBX。

• **公平性讨论**：
  - **jp57**：指出不同人对公平的定义不同，例如有人认为先到先得是公平的，但该项目似乎并未采用这种公平观念。

补充讨论：
• **项目启发与社交邀请**：
  - **nzoschke**：分享了自己制作的类似开源jukebox项目，并邀请原项目作者在Bay Area一起举办Jukebox Happy Hour活动。
  - **lovegrenoble**：提到另一个用于TTRPG（桌面角色扮演游戏）的类似服务Dragonicle。
  - **bahrtw**：建议增加一个可以让访客直接添加可播放歌曲的功能，以增强互动体验。

• **情感反馈**：
  - **noleary**：表示喜欢这个项目是作为“减压项目”的定位。
  - **awaseem**：表达了对开源产品的支持和喜爱。

争议焦点：
• **项目是否侵犯YouTube的服务条款和版权问题**（cdurth的担忧与项目使用YouTube内容的方式之间的争议）。

data.article_summary: 2025年7月8日，格芯（GlobalFoundries）宣布收购MIPS，以增强其在人工智能和计算能力方面的布局。此次收购将扩展格芯的定制IP产品组合，特别是在RISC-V处理器IP和实时计算软件工具方面，应用于自动驾驶、工业自动化、数据中心和智能边缘等领域。MIPS近期推出了基于RISC-V的Atlas处理器IP系列及虚拟优化平台Atlas Explorer，旨在提升性能和效率。格芯表示，收购MIPS将增强其提供灵活的RISC-V开放平台解决方案的能力，并结合其制造技术，助力客户打造更高效的产品。MIPS将成为格芯旗下的独立运营业务，继续服务其客户。收购预计在2025年下半年完成。

GlobalFoundries to Acquire MIPS to Accelerate AI and Compute Capabilities
July 8, 2025
Acquisition will expand GF portfolio with cutting-edge RISC-V processor IP and software tools for real-time computing in autonomous mobility, industrial automation, datacenter and intelligent edge applications
MALTA, N.Y., and San Jose, Calif., July 8, 2025
– GlobalFoundries (Nasdaq: GFS) (GF) today announced a definitive agreement to acquire MIPS, a leading supplier of AI and processor IP. This strategic acquisition will expand GF’s portfolio of customizable IP offerings, allowing it to further differentiate its process technologies with IP and software capabilities.
“MIPS brings a strong heritage of delivering efficient, scalable compute IP tailored for performance-critical applications, which strategically aligns with the evolving demands of AI platforms across diverse markets,” said Niels Anderskouv, president and chief operating officer at GlobalFoundries. “Through this acquisition, we will expand our capabilities to offer customers more flexible, RISC-V-based open platform solutions, paired with our differentiated process technologies and world-class manufacturing to help them build world-class products. This acquisition will be a powerful step forward to push the boundaries of efficiency and performance across a broad range of applications in automotive, industrial and datacenter infrastructure.”
MIPS recently expanded its processor IP offerings, based on open RISC-V specification, with the launch of its Atlas portfolio, a comprehensive suite of compute cores designed for real-time and application processing as well as specialized AI edge processing cores. Additionally, MIPS also introduced Atlas Explorer, a virtual platform that enables optimization of performance, power and area to shift-left in the design cycle.
“Becoming part of GlobalFoundries marks the start of a bold new chapter for MIPS,” said Sameer Wasson, CEO of MIPS. “GF’s proven track record in delivering differentiated technologies through a secure, global manufacturing footprint will enhance our ability to accelerate innovation and scale our solutions—unlocking new opportunities in the Physical AI space and driving even greater value for our customers.”
The acquisition of MIPS is subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including the receipt of required regulatory approvals, and is expected to be completed in the second half of 2025. Following the acquisition, MIPS will continue to operate as a standalone business within GF and serve its customers across a broad range of technologies.
About MIPS
MIPS is the leading provider of compute subsystems for autonomous platforms in automotive, industrial, and embedded markets. With a 40-year heritage in RISC computing innovation and safety capable processing, MIPS is uniquely positioned to simplify the adoption of Physical AI in industrial robotics and automotive applications. MIPS technology is based on the open specification RISC-V instruction set architecture, featuring MIPS pioneering, patented, multi-threaded capabilities to move beyond proprietary legacy architecture lock-ins. For more information, please visit MIPS.com.
About GF
GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors the world relies on to live, work and connect. We innovate and partner with customers to deliver more power-efficient, high-performance products for the automotive, smart mobile devices, internet of things, communications infrastructure and other high-growth markets. With our global manufacturing footprint spanning the U.S., Europe and Asia, GF is a trusted and reliable source for customers around the world. Every day, our talented and diverse team delivers results with an unyielding focus on security, longevity and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com.

data.title: On The Meaning of Ritual
data.author: jger15
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于荀子思想中"礼仪"（ritual）的讨论，及其在现代社会中的应用和意义。

不同观点：
• **buntsai** 同意荀子思想中礼仪的核心地位，但反对作者关于创造新礼仪的建议，认为这种想法自大且天真。他指出，中国在2500年前支撑社会的礼仪实践已经丧失，并质疑创造新礼仪的合理性，提到20世纪极权国家如轴心国通过发明新仪式来操纵社会，并推荐阅读Alasdair MacIntyre的《德性之后》。

• **gerdesj** 对"礼仪"一词的使用持批评态度，认为该词在此处的使用过于宽泛和模糊，甚至带有故弄玄虚的意味。他质疑是否应该将圣经、摩西五经和古兰经等宗教经典也纳入类似讨论。

• **eszed** 认为其他评论者误解了文章中对"礼仪"的定义。文章中的"礼仪"是一个广义的概念，涵盖任何社会行为或社会假设，影响我们的无意识行为。他举例说明，如在没车的情况下闯红灯过马路也是一种"礼仪"。他支持这个广义概念的价值，并认为讨论被对"礼仪"一词的狭义理解带偏了。

• **polivier** 从个人经验出发，强调礼仪带来的心理安慰作用。他分享了自己关于一瓶干邑白兰地的故事，用以说明在重要生活事件中通过特定仪式行为获得的平静和安全感。

• **alganet** 对通过东方哲学文本向西方受众传递智慧持怀疑态度，指出需要警惕某些人利用东方哲学来操纵受众。他质疑如何将所谓的"古老智慧"应用于现代西方生活，并特别提到对将古代智慧直接应用于当代道德和有效统治意识形态的怀疑。

• **indiebat** 认为关于古代仪式或神话的崇高声称并不自动使其变得伟大。他比较了东西方古代智慧，认为通过阅读莎士比亚或蒙田等西方经典可以获得同样的满足感，并质疑对东方哲学的过度神秘化和崇高化。

• **pessimizer** 从经济学角度分析礼仪的作用，认为礼仪是一种浪费资源的表现，通过消耗时间、精力和舒适感来展示对某一原则或目标的承诺。他认为，昂贵的仪式可以防止多重承诺，并通过沉没成本谬误来增强对某一组织的忠诚度。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：关于是否应创造新礼仪的争议，以及对古代礼仪在现代社会中的应用和意义的不同看法。
- **对"礼仪"一词定义的讨论**：评论者对文章中"礼仪"一词的广义使用存在不同看法，有些人认为过于宽泛，导致误解和讨论偏离。
- **东西方哲学的比较**：一些评论者质疑将东方哲学直接应用于西方生活的合理性，并对东方哲学的神秘化表示怀疑。
- **礼仪的心理和社会功能**：有评论者分享了个人经验，强调礼仪在心理安慰和生活事件中的重要性，以及礼仪在社会和组织中的功能。

data.title: Particle Lenia Deluxe Edition
data.author: CraftingLinks
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了**Particle Lenia Deluxe Edition**，一个基于细胞自动机**Lenia**的项目，该项目通过GPU加速实现了3D粒子模拟，支持多物种粒子交互，并引入了多种更新核函数，带来了类似**Particle Life**的复杂行为模式。该项目受Alexander Mordvintsev等人的**Particle Lenia**研究启发，使用**Three.js**和**WebGPU**技术实现。文章简要说明了粒子在能量场中的运动规律，即粒子通过最小化排斥力和最大化生长力来移动，从而产生复杂的行为模式。文中还提供了源代码链接和模拟演示，鼓励读者自行探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[关于Particle Lenia项目及其技术实现的讨论]

不同观点：
• [lbeckman314] 认为该项目非常棒，并分享了如何在Chrome中运行项目的具体步骤，包括克隆仓库、安装依赖和启动开发服务器。他还提供了2D和3D示例的访问链接。
• [UltraSane] 对未来在更强大计算能力（如exaflop计算机）上运行人工生命（alife）研究结果的可能性表示好奇和期待。
• [imiric] 对Lenia的视觉效果表示赞叹，但提到在按照说明操作后，只看到了视频和图片库，并未找到所述的可视化内容，尽管已在Chromium中启用WebGPU。

补充讨论：
• [CraftingLinks] 解释了Particle Lenia项目的技术实现细节，指出该项目使用了Three.js中的计算着色器以及（仍未正式发布的）Three.js着色语言（TSL）。
• 争议焦点：目前没有明显争议，但[imiric]的体验表明项目文档和实际效果之间可能存在不一致，尤其是对于启用了WebGPU的用户。

总结：讨论主要围绕项目的技术实现和运行步骤展开，有人分享使用经验，有人提出未来展望，还有人指出文档与实际效果的潜在不一致问题。

44470447.article_content:
Particle Lenia Deluxe Edition.
Lenia
is a family of cellular automata that produces lifelike behaviors and patterns, first described in the seminal paper by Bert Wang-Chak Chan.
This project is heavily inspired by the original
Particle Lenia
research by Alexander Mordvintsev et al., which implemented a particle-based version of Lenia in Python and
JAX
.
Recognizing the importance of scale (number of particles) for simulation dynamics and iteration times for rapid pattern exploration,
I ported the simulation to the GPU and made it 3D. I also added several update kernels in addition to the original Gaussian one and programmed in
support for multi-species particle simulations which opens up a whole new breed of Mathematical Lifeforms, some that behave very reminiscent to critters found in
Particle Life
.
This port was achieved using compute shaders within
Three.js
and the (still unofficial)
Three.js Shading Language (TSL)
.
You can explore the Particle Lenia universe yourself at the bottom of this post
on the condition that your browser supports
WebGPU
and you have a graphics card with enough muscle to crunch the numbers.
The source code for the Particle Lenia implementation can be found
here
, go wild.
A too short intro to Energy Fields and Particles in Particle Lenia

energy field

where
is the
repulsion field
and
the
growth field
(typically generated by two different convolution kernels). Particles follow the motion law
i.e.
they drift toward lower energy by simultaneously minimizing repulsion
and maximizing growth
. The rich behaviors you see are purely emergent from these local interactions and, to a lesser extent, the choice of kernels (the Mexican-Hat kernel is a personal favorite).
If you’re interested in the math, I encourage you to read the exposition in the original
Particle Lenia paper
.
It only requires that you understand what a ‘gradient’ is (ask an LLM) and how to apply the chain-rule for finding the differential equations.

data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了用于《塞尔达传说：时之笛》存档文件中的16位位集（bitset）实现。该位集用于高效存储大量单比特标志，如"与NPC对话"或"打开宝箱"等状态。位集通过将标志存储在`uint16_t`数组中实现，每个16位字存储16个标志，最多支持4096个字（65536个标志）。其优点包括简单、无依赖、空间高效、快速、可扩展，并且标志ID直观易于调试。文章提供了C和Rust的示例代码及API参考，展示了如何设置、获取和清除位集中的标志。这种方法虽然在技术上不新颖，但因其简洁有效而具有实用价值。

OoT Bitset
The simple, no‑frills flag system used in
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
Implemented in C / C++,
and
Rust
Need to pack
hundreds (or thousands) of one‑bit flags
—“talked to an NPC”, “opened a chest”, etc.—into a save file without wasting bytes?
Ocarina of Time
solved this by storing flags in an array of
uint16_t
words.
oot_bitset
offers the same trick!
I learned about this technique from reading the
OoT decompilation project
source code.  See the
original code
that implements these flags for OoT's save file event information tables.
Why use it?
The bitset used in OoT is the simplest possible implementation of a bitset. It
is not new or novel. It is not fancy or full of features, but it has some nice
properties that is
good enough
for many use cases.
Simple, header‑only, zero deps
– drop a header (C) or add a tiny dependency (Rust). No heap, no
alloc
.
Space‑efficient
– 1 ×
u16
word = 16 flags. Scale from 1 to 4096 words (65 536 flags).
Fast
– branch‑free bit‑twiddling; compiles to a handful of instructions.
Scalable
– need 10 flags or 10 000? Just resize the array.
Intuitive IDs for debugging
– 0x12 maps to first word, second bit.
I wrapped this into a library because I haven't seen this pattern implemented
anywhere, and wanted to have a library I could use in my projects. I also
thought it was a neat bit of OoT lore for software engineer zelda enjoyers.
Why its cool
One clever aspect of how Ocarina of Time uses bitsets is that the first 4 bits
of a 16-bit flag ID directly indicate which bit is set. For example, the
ID 0xA5 means “set the 5th bit of the 10th 16-bit word” — the A (10 in decimal)
selects the 10th word, and the 5 selects the 5th bit within that word.
This works neatly because the word size is 16 bits: 4 bits are enough to index
any bit within a 16-bit word, and it also aligns nicely with a nibble for
debugging. If you switched to 32-bit words, you’d need 5 bits to index the bits
within the word, which no longer fits cleanly into a single nibble.
TL;DR: The flag ID encodes both the word and the bit — it’s the coordinate of the bit!
Bits
15…4
(12 bits)
3…0
(4 bits)
Use
word index
bit index
Max
0–4095 words
0–15 bits
These form a grid, and you can create UIs that visually map these coordinates
to a visual editor:
Hacker news folks say this is not that new or interesting, but I thought it
was! I hope some others find it interesting as well.

data.title: NuxtLabs is joining Vercel
data.author: blinky88
data.article_summary: NuxtLabs宣布加入Vercel，继续致力于打造卓越的开发者体验。Nuxt作为开源框架，将继续保持MIT许可证，社区、公开路线图和核心团队不变。加入Vercel后，Nuxt能够更专注于开源开发，不再为维护和资金分心。未来计划包括发布Nuxt UI v4，免费提供所有Nuxt UI Pro组件和Figma Kit，开源自托管版Nuxt Studio，并使NuxtHub支持更多供应商，无缝集成Vercel的市场服务如Postgres和Redis。此外，Nuxt还将探索AI领域，帮助开发者更快实现想法。所有赞助资金将转移至Open Collective，确保透明和直接支持贡献者。此次合并旨在不损害Nuxt独特性的前提下，推动其进一步发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Vercel收购NuxtLabs及相关框架对开发者社区的影响

不同观点：
• **担忧集中化和独立性丧失**：
   - joshdavham和ayhanfuat表达了对多个流行框架（如Next.js、Svelte/Kit、Nuxt）被Vercel收购后，开发者社区独立性可能受到影响的担忧。ayhanfuat特别提到Vue社区对独立性的重视。
   - meekaaku将这一情况比作Autodesk收购多个3D软件包，担心独立工具会逐渐消失。
   - AbraKdabra担心Nuxt的发展可能会变得更像React，偏离Vue的初衷。

• **支持收购，认为有助于开源可持续性**：
   - danielroe（Nuxt维护者）强调Nuxt的开源愿景和核心价值不会改变，Vercel的支持有助于团队全职从事开源工作，有利于项目的可持续性。
   - strickjb9认为担忧“供应商锁定”是夸大其词，Nuxt仍然可以部署到各种平台，且有资金支持比资源不足导致项目消亡要好。

• **中立但谨慎乐观**：
   - Cu3PO42对去中心化持怀疑态度，但承认资金支持对开源项目的重要性，并对Nuxt的未来持乐观态度。

补充讨论：
• **社区反应和文化问题**：
   - MortyWaves提到Nuxt社区的奇怪氛围和规则，以及对Vercel收购动机的质疑。
   
• **具体影响和后续发展**：
   - aosaigh对Nuxt被Vercel收购感到失望，因为他们选择Nuxt正是因为它不是Vercel的产品。
   - etchalon担心Nuxt对Cloudflare的支持会因收购而终止，导致Vercel成为唯一的一流主机。

• **参考链接**：
   - 提供了更多讨论和公告链接（esher和blinky88），便于进一步了解详情。

总体而言，争议焦点在于收购是否会导致框架独立性和开源精神的丧失，以及对开发者选择和社区文化的潜在影响。

44499860.article_content:
NuxtLabs is joining Vercel
From the start, our mission at NuxtLabs has been to create the best possible developer experience for building fast, beautiful applications. We built Nuxt as an open source framework under the MIT license because we believed that great tools should be accessible, transparent, and community-driven.
We’ve spent years pouring our time, energy, and resources into Nuxt. And through that, we’ve built not just a product, but also a community.
One I’m proud of every single day.
But sustaining open source at this level is hard. With Vercel’s support, we no longer have to split our focus between maintaining Nuxt and funding its future.
Now, we can go all in on what we love: building in the open.
Vercel has a strong history of supporting open source projects and creators: Next.js, Turborepo, Svelte, shadcn, AI SDK, and more. They understand what it means to invest in the web as a shared platform. We’re joining a company that shares our values and is helping us go further without compromising on what makes Nuxt special.
Our open source team is coming along, and
we’ll continue working on Nuxt and Nitro with the same focus and care.
The project stays MIT-licensed. The roadmap stays public. The community stays at the center.
With this, we’re making some changes to how we handle sponsorships. All sponsorship funding will be moved to Open Collective for full transparency and to ensure it goes directly to Nuxt core and community contributors.
What does this mean for you?
Expect to see more open source from us, in the coming months, we will:
Release Nuxt UI v4 with all Nuxt UI Pro components available for free to everyone, as well as our Figma Kit.
Open source a self-hostable version of Nuxt Studio, designed to integrate directly with your Nuxt Content site as an admin to edit your website.
Make NuxtHub agnostic to support other providers, integrating with Vercel’s
Marketplace
offerings like Postgres and Redis will become seamless.
Looking ahead, AI will be a new area of focus for us. We’re exploring how to bring AI into the Nuxt developer experience. Helping you ship ideas faster. We’re also working closely with Vercel’s AI teams, including v0, and continuing to experiment with local tooling like MCP.
Thank you to everyone who’s supported Nuxt along the way. Every contribution, bug report, pull request, and kind word has brought us here. If you have questions or want to join the conversation, Daniel Roe has written about
the future of Nuxt on GitHub
.
We’re still open. Still shipping. And now together with
Vercel
, we’re just getting started.
Sébastien Chopin
NuxtLabs Founder
I’d like to express my gratitude to the people who made this journey possible:
My brother, Alexandre Chopin, for co-founding NuxtLabs back in 2017 when Nuxt was still at version 0.10
Evan You for creating Vue.js and his unwavering support
The entire NuxtLabs team for their years of hard work in building the best developer experience to deliver the best user experience
Guillermo Rauch for bringing this opportunity, Seksom Suriyapa, Baker & McKenzie, and many of the folks at Vercel for making it a reality
Jean-Patrice Anciaux (ISAI), Sam Endecott (Firstminute), Fabien Potencier (Symfony), Eduardo Ronzano (Kolet), and all our investors and angels for their trust
Julia Slama & Kevin de Palmas (JSL Avocats), Paul Jourdan-Nayrac, Sarah Doray, and Donald Davy (Gide), and Joy Sioufi (HL) for their invaluable support and guidance
My wife for her support and patience along the way
And of course, all of you who tried Nuxt, liked it, and shared it with your friends and colleagues 🤍

   - joshdavham和ayhanfuat表达了对多个流行框架（如Next.js、Svelte/Kit、Nuxt）被Vercel收购后，开发者社区独立性可能受到影响的担忧。ayhanfuat特别提到Vue社区对独立性的重视。
   - meekaaku将这一情况比作Autodesk收购多个3D软件包，担心独立工具会逐渐消失。
   - AbraKdabra担心Nuxt的发展可能会变得更像React，偏离Vue的初衷。

• **支持收购，认为有助于开源可持续性**：
   - danielroe（Nuxt维护者）强调Nuxt的开源愿景和核心价值不会改变，Vercel的支持有助于团队全职从事开源工作，有利于项目的可持续性。
   - strickjb9认为担忧“供应商锁定”是夸大其词，Nuxt仍然可以部署到各种平台，且有资金支持比资源不足导致项目消亡要好。

• **中立但谨慎乐观**：
   - Cu3PO42对去中心化持怀疑态度，但承认资金支持对开源项目的重要性，并对Nuxt的未来持乐观态度。

补充讨论：
• **社区反应和文化问题**：
   - MortyWaves提到Nuxt社区的奇怪氛围和规则，以及对Vercel收购动机的质疑。
   
• **具体影响和后续发展**：
   - aosaigh对Nuxt被Vercel收购感到失望，因为他们选择Nuxt正是因为它不是Vercel的产品。
   - etchalon担心Nuxt对Cloudflare的支持会因收购而终止，导致Vercel成为唯一的一流主机。

• **参考链接**：
   - 提供了更多讨论和公告链接（esher和blinky88），便于进一步了解详情。

总体而言，争议焦点在于收购是否会导致框架独立性和开源精神的丧失，以及对开发者选择和社区文化的潜在影响。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Sumble产品的评价与功能建议

不同观点：
• 正面评价：
  ◦ [bittermandel]，[pbmango]，[chsrbrts]，[ohadpr]，[richardmeng]：这些用户对Sumble的UX/UI设计、数据质量和整体表现表示高度赞赏，认为其在同类产品中表现出色。特别是[bittermandel]和[ohadpr]希望保持当前UI不变，认为其已经非常完美。
  ◦ [johnsillings]，[liorsh]：强调了Sumble在GTM（Go-To-Market）策略中的重要性，尤其是在构建客户列表和数据质量方面的优势，但也提到希望增加LLM（大型语言模型）数据处理功能以增强数据转换能力。

• 功能改进建议：
  ◦ [ghc]，[csomar]，[Nivge]：这些用户关注自定义搜索功能、查询速度和数据准确性。例如，[ghc]希望增加自定义搜索选项，[csomar]提到查询速度过慢且数据有时不够准确，[Nivge]则建议引入LLM分类来进行智能过滤。

• 用户体验问题：
  ◦ [marvinkennis]：提到UI存在跳动和自动刷新问题，影响使用体验，并询问如何提供反馈。
  ◦ [ryanrasti]：关注产品是否会扩展到小型公司，暗示目前主要针对中型和大型企业。

• 安全性担忧：
  ◦ [chrisweekly]：提出Sumble可能被垃圾邮件发送者、骗子或网络钓鱼攻击者利用，暗示对产品被不当使用的潜在担忧。

• 技术架构讨论：
  ◦ [rudx]：对Sumble选择知识图谱作为后端的技术决策表示兴趣，并询问其图模型和查询语言的使用情况。

补充讨论：
• 用户普遍对Sumble的数据质量和UX设计表示认可，但也提出了包括查询速度、自定义搜索和数据处理功能等方面的改进建议。
• 部分用户担心UI问题和潜在的安全风险，同时也有用户对产品的技术架构表现出兴趣。
• 总体而言，用户对Sumble的评价较高，但在功能扩展和技术优化方面仍有期待。

data.title: I used o3 to profile myself from my saved Pocket links
data.author: noperator
data.article_summary: 文章主要描述了Pocket服务即将关闭，作者在迁移保存的文章时，发现自己有近900篇文章，时间跨度近7年。通过分析文章的标题、网址、添加时间、标签和状态，作者使用工具xsv对数据进行了简单分析，包括文章数量、时间范围等。随后，作者尝试使用AI助手o3对保存文章的数据进行“画像”推断，得出以下结论：作者可能是一位30-40岁的男性，住在弗吉尼亚州沿海地区，拥有计算机科学学位，担任高级软件工程师，年收入约15万至22万美元，已婚并有多个年幼的孩子。作者在政治上偏向财政保守和公民自由，风险承受能力中等，学习风格以自学为主，信息摄入主要集中在技术、财务、育儿和信仰文化方面。文章还提到作者正从独立技术工作者向技术领导和家庭生活过渡，关注财务独立和退休计划。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用AI分析个人数据（如Pocket存档、浏览历史、聊天记录等）以推测个人特征和兴趣，并讨论其中的技术挑战和应用前景。

不同观点：
• **saeedesmaili**：尝试使用O3、Gemini 2.5 Pro和Opus 4分析Pocket存档数据，发现Opus 4在预测个人信息（如年龄、城市）方面表现最好，但所有模型在职业角色和父母身份预测上都失败了。他指出，结合YouTube观看历史可能会提高兴趣预测的准确性。
• **elcapitan**：从Pocket导出的数据中发现99%的文章是“未读”的，认为这只能说明自己有囤积链接的倾向，对推测其他个人特征持怀疑态度。
• **jackdawed**：讨论了使用AI分析个人数据的技术挑战，如上下文窗口大小和多数据源的追踪问题。提出使用知识图谱来压缩行为模式，并希望出现优化用户效用的AI个人内容推荐系统。
• **benjaminoakes**：提到自己正在开发一个可以帮助分析Pocket数据的工具（https://getoffpocket.com）。
• **fudged71**：使用个性化RSS摘要脚本分析发现，相关性高的RSS feed和实际阅读内容不同。计划开发一个生成“世界模型”来跟踪兴趣和相关信息。
• **gorgoiler**：对LLM输出中的冗余内容感到厌倦，希望有方法可以去除这些冗余，直接获得核心答案。
• **nsypteras**：曾开发一个脚本分析Hacker News（HN）用户的资料，推断其位置、职业、年龄等特征，认为这是一个有趣的实验。
• **asveikau**：提到基于天主教背景推断政治倾向的实验，指出这种推断可能存在偏差。
• **ArturSkowronski**：曾开发一个Pocket分析工具，用于清理和标记数据，并进行分析，认为这是一个情感丰富的实验。
• **stared**：认为十年前简单的机器学习算法已经可以根据少量社交媒体点赞数据预测个性特征，因此对当前深度学习模型的表现持保留态度。
• **frou_dh**：建议使用AI/NLP对Pocket存档进行分类，以便删除不再感兴趣的内容。
• **threecheese**：质疑模型的准确性，指出长上下文问题可能导致结果不全面。
• **IliaLitviak**：开发了一个基于Apple Music听歌历史的推荐系统，发现推荐结果相当不错。
• **cainxinth**：使用LLM分析在线对话者的评论和发帖历史，以判断其是否为 troll，认为LLM可以提供有用的总结信息。
• **hubraumhugo**：开发了一个分析HN账户的工具，认为结果有趣且有时令人害怕。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的技术挑战包括长上下文窗口的限制、多数据源的整合以及知识图谱的构建。
• 有人希望出现优化用户效用的AI个人内容推荐系统，而不是单纯为了广告收入和用户参与度。
• 对LLM输出中的冗余内容和如何去除这些内容也进行了讨论。
• 有人提到结合不同数据源（如YouTube观看历史和Pocket存档）可能会提高兴趣和个性特征预测的准确性。

time_added  1678243022
tags

878

xsv stats | xsv select min,max | xsv flatten |
while read header value; do
echo -n "$header "
date -I -d "@$value"
done
min 2018-07-12
max 2025-06-26
Experiment
#
Recalling Simon Willison’s recent
geoguessing challenge
for o3, I considered, “What might o3 be able to tell me about myself, simply based on a list of URLs I’ve chosen to save?” I opened a temporary chat with o3 (doesn’t use ChatGPT’s memory feature) and prompted:
I’m going to share a list of articles that I’ve saved to Pocket, a read-it-later app. I want you to use that information to “profile” me. Tell me everything about myself that you can possibly infer from this data set. Here’s an example of possible dimensions of that profile, but feel free to include other things that you can infer: age, sex, geographic location, education level, industry/field of work, job level/seniority, income bracket, political orientation, risk tolerance, learning style, information diet, relationship status, parental status and kids’ ages, health concerns, major life transitions, seasonal patterns in interests, etc.
Results
#
o3’s response in full
3

Thought for 13 seconds
The user has shared a broad range of article preferences, which could actually give me some good insight into their demographic and interests. Technical articles related to software, AI, cybersecurity, and finance suggest strong analytical and professional interests. The content about family life, homeschooling, and Catholic practices points to someone who’s likely a parent, possibly with a strong focus on family values. It makes sense to assume they might be male, based on the profiles aggregating to this, but I’m not completely sure yet. I’ll keep this in mind!
I’m pulling together some details! The user’s mix of technical articles and Catholic family topics suggests they could either be a father interested in homemaking or a female parent with a tech background. With a career in software engineering, likely at a senior level, their income probably exceeds 150k. They seem to have a self-directed learning style and a moderate to high risk tolerance in investments. They’re likely married with multiple young kids.

data.title: François Chollet: The Arc Prize and How We Get to AGI [video]
data.author: sandslash
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了与YouTube相关的多项信息和功能。包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻、版权信息、联系方式、创作者相关内容、广告、开发者信息、条款、隐私政策、安全政策、YouTube的工作原理、新功能测试，以及NFL Sunday Ticket等内容。同时，版权归属2025年的Google LLC。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AGI（人工通用智能）的定义及其评估标准，特别是ARC评估测试的作用和意义。

不同观点：
• qoez：认为在ARC测试中取得高分并不意味着拥有AGI，这更多是模式匹配的能力，类似于人类中的不同智力类型，单凭IQ测试不能完全证明一个人的真实智力。
• TheAceOfHearts：指出ARC数据集的预览是亮点，但大部分内容已在其他场合重复过。强调持续学习能力是AGI的重要元素，并提到视频中对抽象库构建的讨论不足。
• stared：不喜欢AGI这个术语，认为 intelligence 总是涉及权衡。ARC高分只是表明AI在某类问题上取得了突破，但不代表一般智力。
• modeless：将ARC-AGI与PuzzleScript游戏类比，建议制作PuzzleScript的AGI benchmark。
• EigenLord：提到No Free Lunch Theorem，认为AGI的追求被金钱驱动而非科学，并怀疑“人类般的智力是否真正通用”。
• visarga：认为智力是搜索，是过去经验与潜在操作区域的转换比率，智力在于模型与环境的相互作用。
• kcaj：引用谈话内容，提出智力是未思考过问题的解决能力，并探讨了General Intelligence定义是否不可计算。
• noiv：质疑o1在Bongard Problems上的表现，并引用相关研究。
• bogtog：认为ARC的视觉特性使其对人类容易而对LLM困难，模型在字符网格解释上表现不佳。
• gtech1：建议将能回答人类无法回答的问题的系统定义为AGI，如调和引力与量子电动力学。
• lawlessone：讨论AGI的定义，认为AGI应是持续 aware 的系统，像生物大脑一样不断更新和存储记忆。
• khalic：认为对AGI的追求可能会造就许多“Cpt Ahab”（执迷不悟的人）。
• chromaton：指出当前AI系统在接受指令和根据世界状态生成新输出方面能力不足，强调有助于AGI进展的基准测试的重要性。

补充讨论：
• ARC评估测试是否能真正衡量AGI存在争议，特别是其在模式匹配和持续学习能力方面的有效性。
• 对AGI定义的多样看法，包括智力类型、持续 aware 能力、及解决人类无法解决的问题的能力。
• 对当前AI系统在特定任务上的表现及其局限性的具体讨论，如字符网格解释和视觉特性任务。
• 对AGI研究动机的质疑，特别是科学与商业驱动之间的平衡问题。

data.title: When Figma starts designing us
data.author: bravomartin
data.article_summary: 本文作者回顾了自2013年首次接触Figma以来的感受，肯定了Figma在远程设计工作中的核心作用，但也表达了对该工具某些功能可能限制设计创造力的担忧。作者特别提到Figma的一些功能，如智能组件、变量、自动布局和交互原型，虽然旨在与工程接轨，却可能过早地限制了设计的自由探索。例如，自动布局虽然方便，但让设计师过早陷入结构化思维，限制了不同布局和创意的尝试。Dev Mode功能则让设计师远离技术细节，花费大量时间在复杂原型上，而这些原型最终往往被丢弃并重新用代码构建。作者认为，设计过程应从草图快速进入代码迭代，而不是追求过早的“开发就绪”。Figma虽然强大，但其强调结构和一致性的功能可能抑制设计的 spontaneity（自发性）和创造性。设计师应警惕这种趋势，确保工具不会悄然重塑和限制他们的实践。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Figma作为设计工具的优缺点，以及其对设计和开发流程的影响

不同观点：
• miiiiiike认为Figma在实现设计系统方面能力不足，特别是在处理多断点、容器查询、模式和变体时表现不佳。他批评Figma过于“设计师化”，导致工程师在实现设计时遇到困难，并最终选择在代码中实现设计系统。
• mananaysiempre则认为Figma的约束是合理的，因为设计需要考虑媒介的限制，尤其是在响应式设计中。他指出，设计师不能忽视这些限制。
• Lalabadie支持miiiiiike的观点，认为Figma在早期探索和研究阶段并不理想，因为它过于关注实施阶段，而忽略了早期探索的需求。
• karaterobot反对miiiiiike对Auto Layout的批评，认为Auto Layout实际上提高了设计效率，使得快速调整布局变得更加容易。
• bbx也支持Figma和Auto Layout，强调其在处理重复项和响应式设计方面的优势。
• pyrale认同miiiiiike的观点，认为设计和开发之间的协作应该更加紧密，而不仅仅是通过高保真模型来传达设计意图。
• samsolomon认为没有理想的工作流程，Figma是否适合取决于团队的规模和合作方式。他指出，在较大的团队中，清晰的组件文档是必要的。
• zelphirkalt批评设计师对网页设计基础知识（如HTML和CSS）的缺乏，认为这是导致不切实际设计的原因。
• asoneth区分了使用既有设计模式和探索新颖设计模式的不同需求，认为Figma适合大多数消费和企业产品设计。
• jjcm（Figma的设计系统PM）部分同意miiiiiike的观点，但认为Figma的目标是同时支持自由形式和结构化设计，并指出Figma的结构化功能是可选的，而非强制性的。
• Separo支持miiiiiike的观点，认为Figma的成功和普及在某种程度上限制了设计的创造性表达。
• travisgriggs分享了与设计外包公司合作的经历，支持miiiiiike对Figma在复杂原型设计中的批评。
• drewbeck不同意miiiiiike的观点，认为工具本身并不决定工作流程，而是由组织和领导决定。他强调Figma在创建一致性界面方面的优势。
• dandano反对miiiiiike的观点，认为Figma的Auto Layout和组件功能极大地提高了设计效率，相比其他工具更加优越。

补充讨论：
• Figma的Auto Layout功能是争议的焦点，有人认为它提高了设计效率，有人则认为它限制了设计的自由表达。
• 设计和开发之间的协作和沟通是另一个重要讨论点，如何在设计工具中平衡这两者的需求是一个持续的挑战。
• 对于Figma是否适合所有设计阶段和工作流程，观点不一，取决于团队规模、合作方式和具体项目需求。
• 设计师对网页设计基础知识的掌握程度也被认为是影响设计工具使用效果的重要因素。

44479502.article_content:
I first encountered Figma in 2013, when Dylan Field demoed an early prototype
to me at O’Reilly’s Foo Camp. I remember the pen tool feeling surprisingly
elegant, but I missed the bigger picture: the radical implications of a design
tool that ran in the browser. A decade later, Figma is a core part of our
creative process, and without it, we wouldn't have been able to build a fully
remote design practice. That’s probably why Dylan is a near-billionaire and
I’m not.
However, over the course of the last five years, I’ve grown increasingly
worried about what Figma is doing to the field of design by pushing designers
toward an engineering-centric way of working. This can be seen in their
feature releases: Smart Components, Variables, Auto Layout, and Interactive
Prototypes. These features are often celebrated as steps toward parity with
engineering, but in practice, they encourage a mode of working that narrows
the field of possibility at precisely the moment when it should be expanding.
A concrete example is Auto Layout. It may seem harmless at first to introduce
a DOM-like layout mechanism in a design tool, and it certainly has advantages
in mature design files where the structure rarely changes. But many design
teams today use Auto Layout to create full page designs of their digital
products from the get-go. In practice, this locks the design in place and
severely limits the possible expressions. You can’t drag things around freely
or try odd combinations of layouts. You can’t simply paste something into a
frame without it snapping to the bottom of the stack. The result is that
designers are nudged into thinking like engineers during the earliest stages
of exploration just when they should be working messily, freely, and loosely.
It might feel convenient at first, but it comes at a cost. Have you ever
opened a Figma file and tried to make a small change, only to find yourself
wrestling with the layout? I’ve encountered this more often than I’d like, and
it seems to be increasing in frequency.
Another feature is Dev Mode, which, in theory, is the missing bridge between
the design specification and the technical implementation. However, it
enforces a mindset where designers polish designs far away from the technology
they are designing for, and where enormous amounts of time are spent on
building complex prototypes, only for them to be discarded and rebuilt in
code. This is all done in the name of making something ready for development.
This is contrary to my belief that any digital design process should start
with rough sketches, but move quickly into code and iterate from there. Those
sketches might even be done in code. A design is never “ready for dev”,
because a lot of what we consider to be design decisions – interaction,
animation, loading of data – can really only be prototyped in code. “Ready for
dev” implies that the creation is done and that the developer is merely there
to execute the designer’s vision, implicitly preventing them from questioning
any of the decisions when the rubber hits the road.
These are just two examples, but it illustrates a worrying trend towards a
premature optimization of design. These features encourage designers to make
decisions too early, to over-structure ideas before they’ve had a chance to
unfold. The result is a narrowing of the design space, where the flexibility
needed for creative discovery is replaced by enforced consistency and
structure. This comes on top of the incredible number of
structured tasks
that most modern design teams adhere to. This inevitably contributes to the
growing monoculture in digital design where everything starts to look and feel
the same, not because of shared intent, but because of shared constraints.
I’ve spent the last 15 years advocating for deeper collaboration between
designers and engineers, so it might seem contradictory to critique a tool
that brings those disciplines closer together. But interdisciplinary work
doesn’t mean collapsing into one way of thinking. The goal isn’t for designers
to adopt engineering practices, but to bring distinct perspectives through an
interdisciplinary way of collaborating.
Figma is extremely powerful, but it is bending us toward a way of working that
prioritizes structure over spontaneity. As designers, we should remain alert
to this shift, not because Figma is inherently bad, but because the values it
encodes can quietly reshape our practices. The best design work rarely starts
with order. It starts with questions, with play, with a lot of mess. We need
tools that make room for that. Because if everything is neatly aligned from
the beginning, we may never discover what lies just outside the grid.

data.title: Adding a feature because ChatGPT incorrectly thinks it exists
data.author: adrianh
data.article_summary: Adrian Holovaty讲述了Soundslice遇到的一个奇怪现象。他们的乐谱扫描系统本应用于将图片形式的乐谱数字化，但近期却收到大量ChatGPT截图，这些截图是ASCII吉他谱。ChatGPT错误地告诉用户，Soundslice支持ASCII谱的音频播放，而实际上该功能并不存在。这导致用户期望落空并对Soundslice产生误解。经过考虑，Holovaty决定开发一个ASCII谱导入工具以满足需求，尽管这并非原计划中的功能。他对这种因误导信息而被迫开发新功能的情况感到复杂，但也乐于帮助用户。这是首个因ChatGPT错误信息而添加功能的案例。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPT-4及LLM（大型语言模型）在编程和产品开发中的应用，特别是它们在API设计、功能开发以及市场研究中的角色和问题。

不同观点：
• **Kragen**：认为利用GPT-4的“幻觉”（hallucination）特性可以帮助改进API的可猜测性和可理解性。通过让GPT-4猜测API如何工作或解释现有代码，可以发现API设计的不足之处。不过，这种方法仅对不特别流行的API有效，且无法解决API效率、可靠性或组合性问题。

• **JimDabell**：支持“幻觉”在测试驱动开发（TDD）中的潜在价值，指出LLM幻觉出的方法或功能有时是合理的，可以作为产品功能开发的启发。

• **Gortok**：对“幻觉”持批评态度，认为依赖AI生成不存在的功能是危险的，尤其是在生成AI本应提供准确信息的场景下。这种“幻觉”可能导致误导用户，并可能产生非良性后果。

• **Shermantanktop**：从音乐符号工具的角度讨论了AI“幻觉”的潜在应用，指出AI可能创造出目前不存在但未来可能有需求的功能，特别是在不同用户群体和需求分裂的领域。

• **Ahstilde**：认为AI的“幻觉”可以帮助识别新用户获取渠道，从而实现产品与渠道的契合（product-channel fit）。

• **Deweller**：关注AI系统通过市场力量影响现实世界的潜力，认为这是AI改变世界的更直接方式，而非通过如机器人控制等极端场景。

• **Jrochkind1**：提出SEO for AI的概念，讨论了如何利用AI聊天机器人引导流量到特定网站的商业潜力，并担心未来可能出现付费推荐的情况。

• **Oasisbob**：指出B2B公司中销售团队快速响应AI幻觉出的新功能的现象，暗示这种做法并不罕见。

• **Simonw**：幽默地指出，实现新功能比让GPT停止“幻觉”更容易，暗示解决AI幻觉问题可能非常复杂。

• **Felixarba**：认为用户不应将GPT的幻觉问题归咎于具体公司，用户应理解这是AI的问题而非服务本身的缺陷。

• **Adambell**：分享了自家AI聊天机器人基于文档进行RAG（检索-增强生成）时也出现了幻觉现象，并将其视为产品反馈的一部分。

44491071.article_content:
Adrian Holovaty
>
Writing
Adding a feature because ChatGPT incorrectly thinks it exists
Written by
Adrian Holovaty
on July 7, 2025
Well, here’s a weird one.
At Soundslice, our
sheet music scanner
digitizes music from photographs, so you can listen, edit and practice. We continually improve the system, and I keep an eye on the error logs to see which images are getting poor results.
In the last few months, I started noticing an odd type of upload in our error logs. Instead of images like this...
...we were starting to see images like this:
Um, that’s just a screenshot of a ChatGPT session...! WTF? Obviously that’s not music notation. It’s
ASCII tablature
, a rather barebones way of notating music for guitar.
Our scanning system wasn’t intended to support this style of notation. Why, then, were we being bombarded with so many ASCII tab ChatGPT screenshots? I was mystified for weeks — until I messed around with ChatGPT myself and got this:
Turns out ChatGPT is telling people to go to Soundslice, create an account and import ASCII tab in order to hear the audio playback. So that explains it!
Problem is, we didn’t actually have that feature. We’ve never supported ASCII tab; ChatGPT was outright lying to people. And making us look bad in the process, setting false expectations about our service.
So that raised an interesting product question. What should we do? We’ve got a steady stream of new users who’ve been told incorrect facts about our offering. Do we slap disclaimers all over our product, saying “Ignore what ChatGPT is saying about ASCII tab support”?
We ended up deciding: what the heck, we might as well meet the market demand. So we put together a bespoke
ASCII tab importer
(which was near the bottom of my “Software I expected to write in 2025” list). And we changed the UI copy in our scanning system to tell people about that feature.
To my knowledge, this is the first case of a company developing a feature because ChatGPT is incorrectly telling people it exists. (Yay?) I’m sharing the story because I think it’s somewhat interesting.
My feelings on this are conflicted. I’m happy to add a tool that helps people. But I feel like our hand was forced in a weird way. Should we really be developing features in response to misinformation?
44491071.article_summary: Adrian Holovaty讲述了Soundslice遇到的一个奇怪现象。他们的乐谱扫描系统本应用于将图片形式的乐谱数字化，但近期却收到大量ChatGPT截图，这些截图是ASCII吉他谱。ChatGPT错误地告诉用户，Soundslice支持ASCII谱的音频播放，而实际上该功能并不存在。这导致用户期望落空并对Soundslice产生误解。经过考虑，Holovaty决定开发一个ASCII谱导入工具以满足需求，尽管这并非原计划中的功能。他对这种因误导信息而被迫开发新功能的情况感到复杂，但也乐于帮助用户。这是首个因ChatGPT错误信息而添加功能的案例。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对初级开发者岗位的影响及技术行业的变化

不同观点：
• [RyanOD] 认为要达到“理解编程基础、架构以及优秀代码的样子”的水平，需要多年实践、协作、研究、犯错和重构，不太可能通过短期学习或使用AI快速达到。
• [Avicebron] 指出，利用AI进行微管理可能导致某些管理者变得更难共事，但这也可能减少模糊、 poorly worded的需求。
• [somanyphotons] 认为初级岗位减少的原因是供应不足，经验丰富的人竞争导致初级开发者机会减少。
• [Anelya] 同意大学课程需要改革以适应快速发展的技术行业，初级岗位职责发生了变化，需要新毕业生具备前沿技能。
• [cadamsdotcom] 认为由于AI的应用，初级开发者的职责和所需知识将向高级开发者靠拢，单人能完成的工作量会增加，这种趋势已持续数十年。
• [coolThingsFirst] 表示大量初级岗位消失，科技行业不再像以前那样有吸引力，依赖AI生成解决方案使得工作变得无趣且缺乏创造性。
• [bigyabai] 质疑AI替代人力（如市场和设计）的效果，认为没有足够的定量数据支持AI能带来成功，反而可能导致市场失败。
• [recursivedoubts] 反问高级开发者从何而来，暗示初级岗位的消失会影响技术人才的培养和晋升。
• [stalfosknight] 认为初级岗位早已消失，招聘时大多只关注已经有“高级”头衔的人，但没人解释高级职位从何而来。

补充讨论：
- AI在技术行业中的应用是否会导致初级岗位减少以及对行业吸引力的影响是讨论的核心。
- 大学教育改革的必要性被提及，以确保新毕业生具备应对行业变化的技能。
- 争议焦点在于AI是否真的能替代人类工作以及其对市场成功的影响，缺乏具体数据支持不同观点。
- 高级开发者培养路径的断层问题也是讨论中值得注意的方面。

Two Chinese satellites have rendezvoused with one another more than 20,000 miles above the Earth in what analysts believe is the first high-altitude attempt at orbital refueling.
China's Shijian-21 and Shijian-25 satellites, known as SJ-21 and SJ-25 for short, likely docked together in geosynchronous orbit sometime last week. This is the conclusion of multiple civilian satellite trackers using open source imagery showing the two satellites coming together, then becoming indistinguishable as a single object.
Chinese officials have released no recent public information on what the two satellites are up to, but they've said a bit about their missions in prior statements.
SJ-25, which launched in January, is designed "for the verification of satellite fuel replenishment and life extension service technologies," according to the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology, the Chinese state-owned contractor that developed the satellite. SJ-21 launched in 2021 and docked with a defunct Chinese Beidou navigation satellite in geosynchronous orbit, then towed it to a higher altitude for disposal before returning to the geosynchronous belt. Chinese officials described this demonstration as a test of "space debris mitigation" techniques.
More than meets the eye
These kinds of technologies are dual-use, meaning they have civilian and military applications. For example, a docking in geosynchronous orbit could foretell an emerging capability for China to approach, capture, and disable another country's satellite. At the same time, the US Space Force is interested in orbital refueling as it seeks out ways to extend the lives of military satellites, which are often limited by finite fuel supplies.
The Space Force sometimes calls this concept dynamic space operations. While some military leaders remain skeptical about the payoff of in-space refueling, the Space Force has an agreement with Astroscale to perform the first refueling of a US military asset in orbit as soon as next year.
China appears to be poised to beat the US Space Force to the punch. The apparent docking of the two satellites last week suggests SJ-21 is the target for SJ-25's refueling demonstration, and US officials are watching. Two of the Space Force's inspector satellites, known by the acronym GSSAP, positioned themselves near SJ-21 and SJ-25 to get a closer look.
Retired Space Force Lt. Gen. John Shaw is a vocal proponent of dynamic space operations. Because of this, he's interested in what happens with SJ-21 and SJ-25. Shaw was deputy commander of US Space Command before his retirement in 2023. In this role, Shaw had some oversight over GSSAP satellites as they roamed geosynchronous orbit.
"The theory behind dynamic space operations stemmed from a kind of operational frustration with our inability to conduct the full range of activities with GSSAP that we wanted to at Space Command, as the warfighter—largely due to the combination of fixed fuel availability and expected satellite lifetime," Shaw told Ars.
As other countries, mainly China, step up their clandestine activities in orbit, military officials are asking more of the GSSAP satellites.
"It was operationally driven then, a couple years ago, but it's now manifesting itself in much wider ways than even it did back then, particularly in the face of activities by potential adversaries," Shaw said. "That’s why I’m more confident and even more zealous about it."
Geosynchronous orbit is a popular location for military and commercial satellites. At an altitude of some 22,236 miles (35,786 kilometers), a satellite's orbital velocity perfectly matches the speed of Earth's rotation, meaning a spacecraft has a fixed view of the same region of the planet 24 hours per day. This is useful for satellites providing military forces with secure strategic communications and early warning of missile attacks.
Now, geosynchronous orbit is becoming a proving ground for new kinds of spacecraft to inspect or potentially attack other satellites. Ground-based anti-satellite missiles aren't as useful in striking targets in high-altitude orbits, and there's a consensus that, if you were to attack an enemy satellite, it would make more sense to use a weapons platform already in space that could move in and connect with the target without blowing it up and creating a cloud of dangerous space junk.
Keeping watch
The US military's GSSAP satellites began launching in 2014. They carry enough propellant to maneuver around geosynchronous orbit and approach objects for closer inspection, but there's a limit to what they can do. Six GSSAP satellites have been launched to date, but the Space Force decommissioned one of them in 2023. Meanwhile, China's satellite operators are watching the watchers.

data.title: Stop forcing AI tools on your engineers
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了管理者不应强制工程师采用AI工具。作者Anton Zaides指出，过度强调AI工具可能导致生产力下降和混乱。他通过反向思维模型提出三种可能导致灾难性结果的做法：1）强制使用AI工具；2）根据AI工具使用量进行评级和晋升；3）完全摒弃传统编码方式。作者强调，管理者的重点应是成果而非工具，应给予工程师时间探索和实验新工具，并根据实际工作情况调整流程。此外，他还建议通过内部成功案例分享来促进合理使用AI工具，而不是盲目跟风。最终目标应是更好地服务客户和推动业务增长。

主要讨论点：AI工具在工作场所的逐步整合及其对人类工作的潜在影响

不同观点：
• 观点一：AI工具的整合是为了逐步取代人类工作。zug_zug认为，公司引入AI工具的每一步（从辅助搜索到自动生成PRs，再到进行根因分析）都是为了让工作流程更加依赖AI，最终可能导致人类工作者被取代。

• 观点二：AI工具的主要目的是提高工作效率，而非取代人类。一些支持引入AI工具的人可能认为，这些工具只是为了提高工作效率和减轻人类工作负担，而不是为了完全取代人类工作者。

补充讨论：
• AI工具在工作场所的应用范围和深度：zug_zug描述了从简单搜索功能到复杂任务（如自动生成PRs和进行根因分析）的演变过程，显示了AI工具在工作场所的应用范围和深度不断扩大。

• 对AI工具的信任和接受程度：zug_zug对AI工具的逐步整合持怀疑态度，认为每一步都在削弱人类在工作流程中的角色。相反，其他支持者可能对AI工具持积极态度，认为这些工具能够有效辅助人类工作，提高生产力。

• 争议焦点：AI工具的引入是否最终会导致人类工作者被取代，或者只是为了提高工作效率。zug_zug的评论反映了对此趋势的担忧，而其他人可能认为这种担忧过于悲观。

Stop forcing AI tools on your engineers
What software engineers really need from their managers right now
Anton Zaides

There is A LOT of pressure in tech.
Every couple of days a new article pops up about how engineers are X% more productive, and how company Y laid off hundreds of developers because they are not needed anymore.
CEOs and executives read this and think:
“Why don’t I see more features released in our company? Our engineers are outdated and they don’t adopt the AI tools fast enough. Let’s become an AI-first company!”.
Well even if it’s not exactly the flow - the result is still that engineers everywhere are pressured to ship faster, adopt the latest tools, and become “AI first”.
And your engineers need their manager to help in that crazy battle.
Let’s start by using my favorite mental model -
Inversion
.
If I wanted to make sure that AI tools adoption would end in a disaster, what would I do?
1. Force it
Cursor is the hot thing right now. So I would forbid all engineers to use IntelliJ/PyCharm.
Also, every new internal tool would have to be built with Bolt or Lovable.
Oh, and we MUST have agents. No more simple API calls. Do we need weather data? Create a ‘Weather agent’ that will get us the info.
The agent thing really drives me crazy. If someone uses the word agent in a vague way in a conversation, I immediately stop listening to them. Don’t call a switch statement with API calls an agent. Nothing wrong with saying ‘code’.
2. Give AI-adoption ratings
Let’s start praising people who adopt the most tools, and use them the most.
We can create a leaderboard, based on tokens used! Oh, and let’s tie the promotions to it - if you didn’t use 10M tokens in a month, you can’t be promoted!
Finally, we have a measurable metric for the next performance review!
You think I’m kidding, but I’ve seen such things on LinkedIn, about how the ‘best’ employees are eating through the tools budget. This is so nuts. Why are we back to praising usage and not outcomes? Let’s measure code lines again!
Goodhart’s law at its best
.
3. Kill the ‘old’ way of writing code
Engineers who write code line by line should be ridiculed. Everyone should develop a habit of asking the AI to do things. If you catch someone updating a log message manually, reprimand them in front of everyone.
AI should write your test. It should debug the production incidents. It should design your screens. No more manual work in our company!
Anton, aren’t you overreacting?
The result of all 3, as I hope you agree with me, will be quite a disaster.
Let’s think about it - what is your goal?
“Become an AI-Native company”?
”Adopt the best tools?”
”Release faster”?
”Show investors you are adapting to AI, to raise your stock price”?
If it’s the latter, nothing I can do about it. But if it’s one of the first three, hopefully the actual goal behind it is to serve your customers better, and grow your business.
Why then would you
focus on tools and not on outcomes?
If you optimize for tools adoption, don’t be surprised if you end up with a slower pace and a complete mess in a year.
Your app is probably already in the
enshitification
phase, maybe you should focus on that first?
So what EMs SHOULD do?
Look, I’m definitely NOT saying that we should ignore those tools. There ARE engineers who are old-fashioned and resist without giving it a real chance. You do have a responsibility to help your team adapt to the new world (and it IS a new world).
But there are so many better ways to do it:
GIVE time to explore
There is no ‘zero’ cost adoption in existing companies. You are not building a todo-list SaaS, where you can spin up a full solution in 30 minutes using Cursor.
Adapting any AI tool to an existing (and big) codebase, is hard, and it takes time. You need to experiment with it during actual work, evaluate what works better, and constantly tweak the flow.
This will hurt in the short run - but you will see a speed increase in the long run, assuming you let people choose the right tools and the right use cases.
Take a couple of enthusiastic engineers, and let them lead this effort. Reduce their workload by 20%, and ask them to play with the latest toys during their work.
Or, take a whole week/month off the roadmap to explore.
Share what worked in YOUR org
Don’t talk about things from other companies - in 90% of the cases it won’t be relevant to you. Instead, understand what worked great in YOUR company, and share that with everyone.
I promise you, most of the engineers are not resistant just for the sake of it, and not for job security. It’s because you can’t really say to Claude ‘improve the performance of our webapp’ and expect something useful.
Yes, you can and should use it to help you debug, analyze, plan, brainstorm. And it IS get

主要讨论点：AI发展的可信度与实际增长情况

不同观点：
• Oras认为，单靠引用那些销售AI技术的公司CEO的观点，并不能为AI的增长提供可信度。他指出，像Zuck这样的CEO也曾花费数十亿美元在AR/VR上，但这些投资并未见到显著成果。因此，Oras建议从其他角度寻找更有说服力的证据，例如AI搜索（如Perplexity、ChatGPT）的增长以及AI应用的下载量（如ChatGPT在iOS上每天有100万次下载）。

补充讨论：
• Oras的观点质疑了依赖行业领袖言论来证明AI技术进步的做法，并提出了具体的数据和实例（如ChatGPT下载量）作为更可信的证据。
• Oras的评论还隐含了对某些技术投资（如AR/VR）未能实现预期回报的批评，暗示对这些技术的乐观预测可能过于夸大。

data.title: The War on the Walkman
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 《被遗忘的随身听之战》一文回顾了1979年索尼随身听发布后引发的社会争议。尽管如今随身听被视为1980年代的象征并引发怀旧情绪，但在当时，它却引起了广泛的不安。批评者如文化评论家Allan Bloom将其视为个人主义的象征，并认为它导致人们从社交中退缩。同时，由于佩戴耳机导致的交通事故风险，美国多个州立法限制在驾驶或骑车时使用耳机，甚至有新泽西州小镇禁止行人佩戴耳机过马路，违者可能面临监禁和罚款。一位退休人员Oscar Gross为此进行公民抗争，但未被判入狱。这一事件反映了新技术往往会遭遇社会抵制的历史现象。文章最后提到，类似的担忧也曾出现在寻呼机的使用上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术对社交互动和人际关系的影响，尤其是耳机和移动设备的影响

🗓️  On this day in 1979 the Sony Walkman was first released, marking its 46th anniversary
The Sony Walkman is now an icon of the 1980s, eliciting nostalgia for the ‘good old days’ of owning music, rather than renting it. Affection for the device is now universal, but that wasn’t always the case…
The sudden rise of headphone wearing pedestrians - spurred by Sony’s lightweight headsets (17% the weight of others) - caused unease about an unfamiliar new world quickly coming into view.
Some said it was a sign of a continued rise of Reagan and Thatcher style individualism. Cultural critic Allan Bloom deemed the Walkman
"a nonstop... masturbational fantasy”
in his 1987 book ‘The Closing of the American Mind.’ Neo-Luddite John Zerzan saw the Walkman as part of a modern trend that encouraged a
"protective sort of withdrawal from social connections"
and Thomas Lipscomb, chief of the Center for the Digital Future, equated it with the euphoric drug "soma," from Huxley's Brave New World, creating, as he put it,
"an airtight bubble of sound"
that was nothing but a
"sensory depressant."
In other words it all felt ‘a bit blackmirror’ as one might say today.
(A collection of quotes collected in this 1999 Reason Magazine
article
)
The Walkman, critics claimed, was more than just music to one's ears; it was a tool of societal disconnect and for government officials and law enforcement a danger on the roads, because it limited the hearing of drivers, cyclists and pedestrians.
After a number of accidents involving Walkman headphones, numerous states across the US swiftly put into effect or proposed restrictions, many related to headphone use while driving or cycling. Among them were statutes in California, Florida, Georgia, , Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and Washington.
The New Jersey township of Woodbridge went a step further, forbidding not just driving or biking, but even crossing the street while wearing Walkman headphones.
The price for breaking this prohibition? A potential two-week stay in jail and a fine. The law made national and international news, including the BBC who got reactions on the street:
The day the law was put into effect - Oscar Gross - a retiree from a neighbouring town, was spurred into action. Seething, he approached Police Sergeant Lou Monzo, purposefully donned his headphones, and crossed the street.
The outcome of this small act of civil disobedience? Gross became the first person to receive a citation for wearing headphones (even though they weren’t plugged into anything.) Undeterred, he stated in an interview,
"I’m prepared to go to jail for 15 days just to prove a point."
Gross end up being interviewed for national outlets as did members of the Woodbridge town council. However, to his disappointment, Gross was not sent to jail. After the judge imposed a $50 fine, which was later suspended, a frustrated Gross said to a journalist:
"He didn't even give me the opportunity to say that I was willing to serve time in jail."
"No municipality has the right to tell somebody what they can wear." -
Oscar Gross
Oscar Gross was
preparing
to take the case all the way to the supreme court, but backed out after someone was killed crossing the street while wearing headphones. The kind of tragic anecdote that is the inevitable and unavoidable price of freedom.
This chapter in techno-pessimism is a good reminder that nostalgia tends to elicit amnesia about the resistance new technologies once faced. After all, who would have thought the “good old days” could ever have been considered a bad, brave new world?

44449970.article_summary: 《被遗忘的随身听之战》一文回顾了1979年索尼随身听发布后引发的社会争议。尽管如今随身听被视为1980年代的象征并引发怀旧情绪，但在当时，它却引起了广泛的不安。批评者如文化评论家Allan Bloom将其视为个人主义的象征，并认为它导致人们从社交中退缩。同时，由于佩戴耳机导致的交通事故风险，美国多个州立法限制在驾驶或骑车时使用耳机，甚至有新泽西州小镇禁止行人佩戴耳机过马路，违者可能面临监禁和罚款。一位退休人员Oscar Gross为此进行公民抗争，但未被判入狱。这一事件反映了新技术往往会遭遇社会抵制的历史现象。文章最后提到，类似的担忧也曾出现在寻呼机的使用上。

data.title: Neanderthals operated prehistoric “fat factory” on German lakeshore
data.author: hilux
data.article_summary: 一项最新研究显示，12.5万年前生活在中德地区的尼安德特人使用了一种先进的食品加工方法，即利用水和热系统性地从大型动物骨骼中提取脂肪。这一发现出自在Neumark-Nord 2的考古遗址，表明尼安德特人对营养、计划和资源管理有着更为先进的认识。研究显示，他们不仅砸碎骨头获取骨髓，还将其粉碎并煮沸以提取富含营养的骨脂。该遗址出土了至少172只大型哺乳动物的遗骸，表明这种生产骨脂的活动是经过精心组织和战略性进行的。这一发现改变了我们对尼安德特人饮食和适应能力的理解，展示了他们高度复杂的生存策略和环境管理能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：尼安德特人提取骨脂的技术及其相关能力（如语言、合作等）的讨论

不同观点：
• **关于煮沸技术的质疑与解释**：
  - [jbotz] 提出疑问：尼安德特人如何在没有陶器的情况下煮沸骨头以提取脂肪？随后通过研究发现，可以使用动物皮或桦树皮等耐燃材料，只要水位保持足够高，材料就不会超过100摄氏度。这挑战了以往古人类学认为人类在陶器发明前无法煮沸的假设。
  - [octaane] 补充了其他简单方法，如挖洞加热水和石头，或者直接倒入煮沸的水，展示了尼安德特人可能采用的多种方法。

• **关于尼安德特人智慧和语言能力的讨论**：
  - [Roark66] 认为尼安德特人能够进行复杂的协作和计划，质疑过去关于他们没有语言能力的假设，指出如果无法沟通意图和计划，他们不可能完成提取骨脂等复杂任务。
  - [samuell] 简单提到，尼安德特人是人类的一部分，暗含他们具备类似现代人类的智力水平。

• **对研究结论的质疑**：
  - [poulpy123] 认为研究中的结论有夸大之嫌，指出尼安德特人对脂肪营养价值的理解并不比其他食肉动物或早期人类更优越，这仅仅是进化驱动的行为。

• **文化传播的假设**：
  - [baxtr] 猜测现代人类可能从尼安德特人那里学会了骨脂提取技术，因为该技术以前被认为仅限于晚期智人。

补充讨论：
• **对AI生成图片的评论**：
  - [qoez] 提到在评论中看到的图片似乎是AI生成的，并指出了AI生成图片的一些特征。

• **幽默评论**：
  - [tpoindex] 分享了一张幽默图片，调侃尼安德特人提取骨脂的活动。
  - [FooBarBizBazz] 以幽默方式将骨脂提取过程比作做汤，并好奇他们使用的调料。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于尼安德特人是否具备足够的智慧和技术（如语言能力）来进行复杂的食物加工活动，以及过去学术假设的可靠性。

44460498.article_content:
Neanderthals in central Germany 125,000 years ago employed an advanced method of food preparation, according to a recent study: systematically stripping fat from the bones of large animals using water and heat. The practice, uncovered at the Neumark-Nord 2 archaeological site, shows that Neanderthals had a much more advanced conception of nutrition, planning, and resource management than previously believed.
Artistic impression of activities at the “Fat Factory” site. Credit: Scherjon, LEIZA-Monrepos
The research, published in Science Advances, was conducted by international researchers from MONREPOS (Leibniz Centre for Archaeology), Leiden University in the Netherlands, and the State Office for Heritage Management and Archaeology of Saxony-Anhalt. The study indicates that Neanderthals, in addition to smashing bones to access the marrow—a behavior shared by their earliest African ancestors—also crushed them into fragments and boiled them to obtain bone grease, a nutrient-rich resource.
“This was intensive, organized, and strategic,” said Dr. Lutz Kindler, the study’s lead author. “Neanderthals were clearly managing resources with caution—planning hunts, transporting carcasses, and rendering fat in a task-specific area. They understood both the nutritional value of fat and how to access it efficiently.”
Excavations at the Neumark-Nord 2 site. Credit: Wil Roebroeks, Leiden University
At least 172 large mammals, such as deer, horses, and aurochs, were butchered here. The production of bone grease, which required huge quantities of bone to be worthwhile, was previously considered to be something limited to Upper Paleolithic modern humans. This find pushes back the timeline by thousands of years and represents a fundamental shift in our knowledge of Neanderthal diet and adaptation.
From complete bones to tiny fragments. Credit: Kindler, LEIZA-Monrepos
The Neumark-Nord complex, discovered in the 1980s by archaeologist Dietrich Mania, is a full interglacial ecosystem. Excavations from 2004 to 2009 revealed several zones with various Neanderthal activities: deer hunting and light butchering in one, straight-tusked elephant processing in another, and fat removal in a third, specialized area. Remarkably, cut-marked remains of 76 rhinos and 40 elephants were also discovered at nearby sites like Taubach.
Related
Stories
Fried thrushes were ancient Roman street food in Mallorca, not just an elite delicacy
June 11, 2025
43,000-year-old Neanderthal fingerprint discovered on stone is the world’s oldest
May 30, 2025
“What makes Neumark-Nord so exceptional is the preservation of an entire landscape, not just a single site,” said Leiden University’s Prof. Wil Roebroeks. “We are seeing a range of Neanderthal behaviors within the same landscape.”
Massive bone processing. At the Neumark-Nord 2 site, near the margin of a shallow pool, there is a dense concentration of bones from more than 170 larger mammals (highlighted in blue), mixed with flint
artifacts
(red) and hammer stones (red). Credit: Kindler, LEIZA-Monrepos
The activities of the Neanderthals at Neumark-Nord not only demonstrate high sophistication but were also likely to have long-term environmental impacts. Prof. Roebroeks warned that their mass hunting of slow-reproducing species undoubtedly left a significant impact on fauna in the region during the Last Interglacial period.
The finds depict the Neanderthals as more capable and more intelligent than the stereotype of the brutish caveman. The “fat factory” at Neumark-Nord reveals a species that could plan for the future, manage its environment, and maximize nutrition in resource-poor environments.

data.title: Intel's Lion Cove P-Core and Gaming Workloads
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: Intel's Lion Cove P-Core架构在指令每周期（IPC）和能效方面相比前代Raptor Cove有显著提升，尤其在SPEC CPU2017基准测试中表现优异。然而，在游戏负载下，其IPC表现较低，主要受限于前端和后端延迟。通过自顶向下分析发现，后端内存延迟是导致流水线槽利用不足的主要原因，而错误预测和前端带宽问题较小。Lion Cove采用四级数据缓存设计，L1.5缓存在一定程度上缓解了L2的压力，但命中率一般。尽管L2缓存有效减少了L3的访问，但访问L3和DRAM的延迟仍然较高，影响性能。测试使用了Core Ultra 9 285K处理器和DDR5-6000内存，游戏包括《Cyberpunk 2077》和《Palworld》。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• [onli] 引用多代CPU的基准测试数据，指出测试的CPU（285K）在游戏性能上落后于Intel前两代的高端处理器（i7-13700K、i9等）以及一些AMD处理器，强调3D缓存在游戏中的重要性，并认为新一代CPU在游戏性能上不如其前代产品。

Lion Cove is Intel’s latest high performance CPU architecture. Compared to its predecessor, Raptor Cove, Intel’s newest core can sustain more instructions per cycle, reorganizes the execution engine, and adds an extra level to the data cache hierarchy. The list of changes goes on, with tweaks to just about every part of the core pipeline. Lion Cove does well in the standard SPEC CPU2017 benchmark suite, where it posts sizeable gains especially in higher IPC subtests. In the Arrow Lake desktop platform, Lion Cove can often go head-to-head against AMD’s Zen 5, and posts an overall lead over Intel’s prior Raptor Cove while pulling less power. But a lot of enthusiasts are interested in gaming performance, and games have different demands from productivity workloads.
Here, I’ll be running a few games while collecting performance monitoring data. I’m using the Core Ultra 9 285K with DDR5-6000 28-36-36-96, which is the fastest memory I have available. E-Cores are turned off in the BIOS, because setting affinity to P-Cores caused massive stuttering in Call of Duty. In Cyberpunk 2077, I’m using the built-in benchmark at 1080P and medium settings, with upscaling turned off. In Palworld, I’m hanging out near a base, because CPU load tends to be higher with more entities around.
Gaming workloads generally fall at the low end of the IPC range. Lion Cove can sustain eight micro-ops per cycle, which roughly corresponds to eight instructions per cycle because most instructions map to a single micro-op. It posts very high IPC figures in several SPEC CPU2017 tests, with some pushing well past 4 IPC. Games however get nowhere near that, and find company with lower IPC tests that see their performance limited by frontend and backend latency.
Top-Down View
Top-down analysis
characterizes how well an application is utilizing a CPU core’s width, and accounts for why pipeline slots go under-utilized. This is usually done at the rename/allocate stage, because it’s often the narrowest stage in the core’s pipeline, which means throughput lost at that stage can’t be recovered later. To briefly break down the reasons:
Bad Speculation: Slot was utilized, but the core was going down the wrong path. That’s usually due to a branch mispredict.
Frontend Latency: Frontend didn’t deliver any micro-ops to the renamer that cycle
Frontend Bandwidth: The frontend delivered some micro-ops, but not enough to fill all renamer slots (eight on Lion Cove)
Core Bound: The backend couldn’t accept more micro-ops from the frontend, and the instruction blocking retirement isn’t a memory load
Backend Memory Bound: As above, but the instruction blocking retirement is a memory load. Intel only describes the event as “TOPDOWN.MEMORY_BOUND_SLOTS” (event 0xA4, unit mask 0x10), but AMD and others explicitly use the criteria of a memory load blocking retirement for their corresponding metrics. Intel likely does the same.
Retiring: The renamer slot was utilized and the corresponding micro-op was eventually retired (useful work)
Core width is poorly utilized, as implied by the IPC figures above. Backend memory latency accounts for a plurality of lost pipeline slots, though there’s room for improvement in instruction execution latency (core bound) and frontend latency as well. Bad speculation and frontend bandwidth are not major issues.
Backend Memory Access
Lion Cove has a 4-level data caching setup, with the L1 data cache split into two levels. I’ll be calling those L1 and L1.5 for simplicity, because the second level of the L1 lands between the first level and the 3 MB L2 cache in capacity and performance.
Lion Cove’s L1.5 catches a substantial portion of L1 misses, though its hitrate isn’t great in absolute terms. It gives off some RDNA 128 KB L1 vibes, in that it takes some load off the L2 but often has mediocre hitrates. L2 hitrate is 49.88%, 71.87%, and 50.98% in COD, Palworld, and Cyberpunk 2077 respectively. Cumulative hitrate for the L1.5 and L2 comes in at 75.54%, 85.05%, and 85.83% across the three games. Intel’s strategy of using a larger L2 to keep traffic off L3 works to a certain extent, because most L1 misses are serviced without leaving the core.
However, memory accesses that do go to L3 and DRAM are very expensive. Lion Cove can provide an idea of how often each level in the memory hierarchy limits performance. Specifically, performance monitoring events count cycles where no micro-ops were ready to execute, a load was pending from a specified cache level, and no loads missed that level of cache. For example, a cycle would be L3 bound if the core was waiting for data from L3, wasn’t also waiting for data from DRAM, and all pending instruction

data.title: Bootstrapping a side project into a profitable seven-figure business
data.author: jonkuipers
data.article_summary: Kyle Nolan分享了他通过自力更生（bootstrapping）将副业ProjectionLab发展成一个年收入达100万美元的成功企业的历程。从2021年开始，Kyle受财务独立运动启发，因找不到合适的财务规划工具而自行开发ProjectionLab。经过四年的努力，从最初每月150美元的收入增长到2025年的83.3K美元。这一路充满了挑战和情绪波动，Kyle多次想要放弃，但最终通过坚持和组建团队取得了成功。他强调，创业过程如同乘坐过山车，而“不放弃”是成功的关键。Kyle还分享了找到合适的增长与营销伙伴Jon Kuipers，并逐渐建立团队，使企业持续增长的经验。最终，ProjectionLab不仅帮助了超过10万家庭规划财务未来，也实现了Kyle自己的财务独立目标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：创业过程中的坚持与固执的界限、市场验证的重要性、营销的作用、利润与收入的区别以及国际市场的关注。

不同观点：
• bruce511认为，在坚持与固执之间找到平衡非常困难，市场验证对于确保走在正确的道路上至关重要。他强调了营销的作用，如写博客和维护Discord服务器，这些可能比编写代码本身更重要。
• rorylaitila分享了自己的经验，表示只能构建和销售自己经常使用的产品，以避免信号弱和倦怠问题。这种自我验证的方法对他来说是有效的。
• montakaoh对收入波动有共鸣，描述了互联网收入带来的过山车般的感觉，但承认自己尚未达到同样的成功水平。
• mdorazio对没有提到利润表示失望，强调收入不等于利润，指出很多创始人在追求收入时忽视了实际可支配收入的重要性。
• ipaddr对市场验证的具体含义提出疑问，质疑从第一笔销售到多次收入波动之间的验证过程，质疑单凭少数用户支付是否能验证大规模市场需求。
• braden-lk关注增长营销人员的寻找和适配问题，询问如何找到合适的营销人才。
• davidw将项目比作“向矿工卖铲子”，认为这是一种服务于特定需求的创业方式，而不是对项目的批评。
• noisy_boy询问业务是否专注于美国客户，或者是否也涵盖国际客户。
• artur_makly对项目表示赞赏，并表示自己原本打算自己做一个类似的东西，但最终选择支持其他创业者。
• akomtu表示对创业中的错误和不同做法的兴趣，希望了解更多反思和改进建议。

补充讨论：
• rvz强调每天坚持工作的重要性，认为这是最简单却也最难做到的事情，尤其是不间断的每日坚持。
• joak提到幸存者偏差问题，指出失败的创业经历通常不会被广泛报道，成功故事更易被看到。

这些评论反映了创业过程中的多方面挑战和策略，包括市场验证、营销、利润与收入的平衡以及国际市场的考虑。争议的焦点主要在于市场验证的标准和利润与收入的区别。

We reached $1M ARR with zero funding
Kyle Nolan

Jun 30, 2025
Bootstrapping a side project into a profitable seven-figure business in four years.
We really did it! We bootstrapped ProjectionLab to $1,000,000 in annual recurring revenue.
And I’m still processing that this is real. 🥹
Back in 2021, I was inspired by the financial independence movement and wanted a better way to plan my own life. I couldn’t find the right tool, so I started building.
I had no idea that side project would one day help over 100,000 households plan for their financial future too.
How we got here
If this is your first time hearing about ProjectionLab, here’s a quick recap:
Milestone

What Was Happening

post to HN
)

Started to believe I could do this

The final boss of indie hacking

Quit my day job and went all-in!
$41.6K MRR

Started growing the team
$45.8K MRR
Aug 2024
Shared story on ChooseFI
$83.3k MRR
Jun 2025
👋 Here we are!
When you look beyond the recurring revenue chart, this journey had ups, downs, and moments I wanted to quit.
The emotions behind the numbers
Want to know what building in public from zero to a million dollars a year really felt like? NOT like serenely progressing up-and-to-the-right…
More like riding a dopamine rollercoaster while getting attacked by a bear.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
The flat months in the early years? The dips in earnings? The times I woke up to a dozen canceled subscriptions?
Each one had me questioning everything, wondering if I should just focus on the corporate ladder, or maybe try to get into big tech instead.
The financial independence movement is what set me on this path. So on top of worrying about normal business risks, I was primed to think in terms of my time and opportunity cost, and how failure would hurt my own timeline to FI.
But gradually, I learned that emotional peaks and valleys are always a part of entrepreneurship. And that “not giving up” is actually a superpower.
Not giving up
There are loads of people out there smarter than me.
But luckily, success indexes less on IQ and more on consistency. The willingness to doggedly show up every single day can take you to some really suprising and amazing places.
And you know what makes it easier and more rewarding to be that persistent?
Working alongside people you like.
From solo dev to real team
For the first two years, I burned the candle at both ends working solo. 4-6 hours every night after work, entire weekends, holidays, you name it.
404 Day Off Not Found.
That was the only way I could build something this complex in a crowded market as a risk-averse engineer with a day job. And I was fortunate enough to attempt this at a stage in life when I had lots of energy and few family responsibilities.
Plus my trusty sidekick, BB the bird:
But long-term, I knew there would be a choice to face:
Keep doing everything myself and watch growth plateau, or…
Find someone with a complementary skillset and start building a team.
I was just an ordinary engineer with zero marketing experience. So I figured I should try to team up with someone good at growth & marketing.
Finding a growth & marketing partner
During the first few years, I was approached by dozens of potential “partners.” Several wanted an outsize equity stake to essentially just make suggestions. Others had the wrong skillset or didn’t feel like a complete fit.
But
Jon Kuipers
jumped right into the trenches and worked to prove himself before asking for anything. He spent a year contributing real value, and when the time came to bring on a growth partner full-time, I didn’t look anywhere else.
Now I stay focused on building, while he handles growth, marketing, partnerships, and some ops stuff.
Building a team
We’ve also added a few contractors to the team.
And these guys are legends. 💪
They come straight from the ProjectionLab user community, and they are doing a great job fielding the arcane finance questions our customers love to ask. Plus hosting 1-on-1 sessions, creating
tutorial videos
, and more.
Could we have offshored customer success for pennies on the dollar instead? You bet. But having a happy and engaged user community of product evangelists means a lot to us, and I want them all to have the best experience possible.
For multiple years, I was up at all hours answering support questions myself. It interrupted my dev work (and my sleep) constantly. I love the PL community – it’s a big part of what motivated me to keep going back then.
And it blows my mind that the empty discord

• ipaddr对市场验证的具体含义提出疑问，质疑从第一笔销售到多次收入波动之间的验证过程，质疑单凭少数用户支付是否能验证大规模市场需求。
• braden-lk关注增长营销人员的寻找和适配问题，询问如何找到合适的营销人才。
• davidw将项目比作“向矿工卖铲子”，认为这是一种服务于特定需求的创业方式，而不是对项目的批评。

• artur_makly对项目表示赞赏，并表示自己原本打算自己做一个类似的东西，但最终选择支持其他创业者。
• akomtu表示对创业中的错误和不同做法的兴趣，希望了解更多反思和改进建议。

data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了状态空间模型（SSM）和Transformer在序列建模中的权衡，特别关注SSM的三个关键要素：状态大小、状态表达力和训练效率。首先，状态大小决定了模型能存储多少上下文信息，SSM通过更大的隐藏状态向量提升了信息存储能力。其次，状态表达力要求模型能灵活选择和编码重要信息，现代SSM如Mamba通过动态变换矩阵增强了表达力。最后，训练效率涉及计算复杂性和内存管理，Mamba通过算法创新实现了高效的并行计算和内存使用。尽管这些要素并非全新，但Mamba通过将它们有效结合，提升了SSM在语言建模上的性能，使其能与Transformer媲美。
